title: B2B Ordering Platform for Food Wholesale Business (WooCommerce/WordPress)
description:
Overview:
We are a food wholesale company (supplying smashburger and fast-food items to horeca/restaurant businesses in the Netherlands) currently taking orders via WhatsApp. We want to move to a professional online B2B ordering platform for our ~25 existing business customers, built to scale as we grow.

What we need:

A WordPress + WooCommerce website with a public-facing company page and a secure customer login portal
B2B functionality: each customer logs in and sees their own individually negotiated prices/discounts (via a B2B plugin such as B2BKing or Wholesale Suite)
Product catalog setup: fast-food items (burgers, sauces, packaging) with appropriate units (pieces, boxes, kg)
Custom checkout logic: customers choose between (a) pay immediately (iDEAL/card) and receive a 5% discount, or (b) order on invoice/account with a 14-day payment term at full price
Integration with Dutch accounting software (Moneybird or e-Boekhouden.nl) so orders automatically generate invoices with the correct pricing/discount and payment terms applied
Automatic packing slip (pakbon) generation for each order, for warehouse fulfillment
Clean, professional design; mobile-friendly

Scope of work / phases:

WordPress + WooCommerce base site setup
E-mail addresses for three partners
B2B plugin configuration with individual customer pricing (25 accounts to set up)
Custom checkout logic for the prepay-discount vs. invoice-on-account flow
Accounting software integration (auto-invoicing)
Packing slip automation
Testing and go-live support (migrating customers from WhatsApp to the portal)

Nice to have:

Experience with Dutch VAT/invoicing requirements
Experience with food/wholesale/distribution businesses

Timeline: Looking to launch within 2 weeks.

Budget: Open to fixed-price or hourly proposals — please quote based on the scope above.

To apply, please include:

Relevant past projects (especially WooCommerce B2B or wholesale ordering platforms)
Your estimated timeline and cost breakdown by phase
Your experience with Moneybird or e-Boekhouden.nl integrations, if any
coverLetter:
Hi! Moving your fast-food wholesale operations smoothly from WhatsApp to a dedicated WordPress and WooCommerce B2B portal is right in my wheelhouse. 

I regularly build secure, high-performance WooCommerce B2B platforms featuring tiered/individual customer pricing, advanced checkout conditional logic (like applying a 5% discount for iDEAL prepayments versus net-14 invoices), and automated packing slip generation. For Dutch market requirements, I am well-versed in configuring local payment gateways, VAT rules, and ERP/accounting integrations like Moneybird and e-Boekhouden.nl to ensure your orders seamlessly trigger automated invoicing. You can review a sample of my complex WordPress and WooCommerce implementations here: https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/

I can easily meet your 2-week launch timeline. Let's chat about your ~25 accounts and kick this off—are you currently leaning toward Moneybird or e-Boekhouden.nl for your accounting sync?

title: WooCommerce Fraud & Security Specialist
description:
We're hiring an experienced WooCommerce fraud and security specialist to stop an ongoing automated card-testing attack on our store.

For several weeks, bots have been submitting waves of checkout attempts, mostly on low-priced products. Most were declined, but some recent ones went through, creating real financial and chargeback risk. Our existing defenses are being bypassed.

Scope of work:

Investigate how fraudulent transactions got through and close the gap without disrupting legitimate customers.
Audit our checkout, payment gateway, Cloudflare/WAF, and WordPress security settings, and explain what's working and what isn't.
Implement a durable, proven long-term solution to prevent recurrence.
Deliver documentation of the root cause and changes made, plus a runbook for future attacks.

Requirements:

Direct experience resolving WooCommerce card-testing attacks
Strong knowledge of WooCommerce, payment gateway fraud controls, Cloudflare, and WordPress security
Comfortable with SSH, WP-CLI, and log analysis, and careful with changes to a live production site
Able to start immediately and be available during US business hours

To apply: Please briefly describe a past WooCommerce card-testing or payment-fraud case you handled, including the cause and how you resolved it.
coverLetter:
Hi! To answer your question: on a recent WooCommerce project experiencing an automated card-testing attack, bots were exploiting a lack of rate limiting and missing CAPTCHA on guest checkouts, bypassing basic gateway rules. I resolved it by implementing advanced Cloudflare WAF custom firewall rules (challenging suspicious JA3 fingerprints and ASN patterns), integrating reCAPTCHA v3 invisibly into the WooCommerce checkout flow, and adding strict IP rate-limiting via server-level configurations. This completely stopped the fraudulent volume within hours without impacting legitimate customer conversions.

I am an experienced WordPress and WooCommerce security specialist comfortable with SSH, WP-CLI, and deep log analysis to safely audit your live production site. I can immediately investigate your gateway, Cloudflare, and WP security layers to close the vulnerability gap and provide the requested runbook.

Are you available for a quick chat today to get started on stopping these attacks?

title: Amendments to Wordpress website webshop
description:
Hi, I require the following changes and improvements to be implemented on my webshop: atelierchristian. 

1. Product Filtering System
The webshop needs a user-friendly filtering system. See for example ‘https://www.bol.com/nl/nl/l/heren-sieraden/47120/’ or ‘https://juweelwinkel.nl/sieraden/’

1.1 This needs to be a widget, so that I can place it on the left-hand side of the webshop/category pages or wherever else I want to place it (in an adjusted form). Of course, it needs to work on desktop and should also work properly on mobile devices.

1.2 I need to be able to make any filter system that I want based on the tags already present on the website. This product page has several tags, such as “Tags: 18 karaat, Christian fine ring, Dames, Dames ring, Diamant, Geel Goud, Geel gouden ring”. Thus, the filter system needs to align with this. 

1.3 I need to be able to choose within the filter system whether I want it to be a check-box, a plain text or an image that I can upload. I must also be able to put there a separate link if I want to (e.g. a webpage that is not a tag), other than a tag. 

1.4 There needs to be a ‘see more’ function, in other to prevent the filter system being too long. I need to be able to add, remove, rename etc. new filter options. The filter system should therefore be expandable in the future.

1.5 Needless to say, there must a price filter. Going from € 0,- to the highest price at the time. The filter system must automatically align with the products already available on the website. I want the option to exclude automatically all sold products from the list of products that the filter system shows – or, when I change my mind, to include them.

1.6 Of course, combinations of filters must be possible. E.g., men, yellow gold, ring, with diamond etc. The product results should update immediately without unnecessarily reloading the entire page.

1.7 There should also be a clear “Reset/Clear Filters” option.

2. Permanent Search Bar
The current search icon/magnifying glass should be improved. 

I want a complete search bar that is permanently visible in the website header.
 


The search function should search through the webshop product information, as it does now. Including:
•	Product names
•	Product categories
•	Product descriptions
•	Materials
•	Gemstones
•	Relevant product information/SKU where applicable
If possible, use live search/autocomplete so customers can already see relevant products while typing.


3. Sold-Out Products – Remove Add to Cart
When a product is out of stock, the green “Add to Cart” button must automatically disappear or become unavailable. This should happen automatically based on the product's stock status. A customer must never be able to accidentally order a product that is marked as unavailable unless that specific product is intentionally configured as a backorder product.

4. Sold-Out Products – Restock / Product Request
When a product is sold out, replace the normal purchasing option with a clear button such as: “Product aanvragen”. When clicking the button, the customer must submit: 
•	Name
•	Telephone number
•	Email address
The request must be linked to the specific product. info @ atelierchristian . nl should then receive the request by email and preferably also be able to see the request in the website backend.
The request should clearly show:
•	Customer name
•	Telephone number
•	Email address
•	Product name
•	Product/SKU
•	Date of request
If possible, the system should also allow an automatic email notification to the customer when the product becomes available again.

6. General Requirements
All new functionality must:
•	Work properly on desktop
•	Work properly on mobile phones
•	Work properly on tablets
•	Be easy and clear for customers to use
•	Match the existing Atelier Christian website design
•	Not unnecessarily slow down the website
•	Work correctly with existing products and product pages
•	Be SEO-friendly where relevant
•	Be expandable in the future
Before final implementation, please make sure that the filtering, search and stock request functions are properly tested.

7. Remove fake users

A lot of fake user accounts have been made on my website. Can you please remove these, whilst keeping the actual accounts of the real users? And prevent that this happens again?
coverLetter:
Hi! I can help you implement all these improvements for your WooCommerce webshop, Atelier Christian, ensuring a seamless experience on both desktop and mobile.

To address your requirements:
1. **Advanced Filtering & Search:** I will set up a flexible, AJAX-powered sidebar filter matching your exact tag structure, including custom image/text options, price ranges, sold-out toggles, and instant multi-filter results without page reloads. I'll also upgrade your header with a live autocomplete search bar.
2. **Stock & Restock Management:** I'll configure the out-of-stock logic to remove the "Add to Cart" button and replace it with a custom "Product aanvragen" inquiry form that logs requests directly to your backend and emails info@atelierchristian.nl.
3. **Security:** I'll clean out the spam user accounts and implement robust security hardening to prevent future fake registrations.

You can see examples of my recent WordPress and WooCommerce work here: https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/. 

When would you like to get started?

(link removed)/

About the Project
We are seeking an experienced WordPress + Elementor Pro developer to implement and launch a complete 27-page website for One Love Humanity (OLH), an Australian organisation working across human development, mental health and NDIS supports, organisational services, professional development, programs and community engagement.
This is not a website design project starting from scratch.
A substantial amount of the strategy, architecture, copywriting, design specification and front-end planning has already been completed.
We are looking for a developer who can take this completed system and translate it accurately and efficiently into a native, reusable WordPress + Elementor Pro website.
What Has Already Been Completed
We will provide the successful developer with a comprehensive development package, including:
- Complete 27-page website architecture and URL structure
- Approved website copy
- Defined brand and visual design system
- Exact colours and typography
- Responsive design rules
- Global navigation and footer structure
- Reusable page/component architecture
- Visual Asset Placement Register
- Contact Hub specification and enquiry pathways
- Program, service and team/profile page structures
- Five completed HTML/CSS reference pages
- Detailed developer handoff documentation
- Static/source QA documentation
The five reference pages represent key page types and are intended to establish the reusable visual and structural system for the remaining website.
The successful developer should therefore not approach this as 27 unrelated page designs.
The objective is to establish the global WordPress/Elementor system, reusable templates, containers and components first, and then efficiently scale that system across the remaining pages.
Scope of Work
The project includes implementation of the complete 27-page website, including:
- WordPress implementation
- Elementor Pro implementation
- Responsive desktop, tablet and mobile layouts
- Global header, navigation and footer
- Global colours and typography
- Reusable Elementor containers, templates and components
- Program pages
- Service pages
- Team/profile pages
- Contact Hub and enquiry forms
- Form routing and enquiry pathways
- MailerLite integration
- Acuity Scheduling integration
- Technical/on-page SEO setup
- Appropriate page titles and metadata implementation
- Sitemap
- Appropriate structured data/schema where required
- Accessibility implementation targeting WCAG 2.2 AA
- Performance optimisation
- Cross-browser and cross-device QA
- Staging/testing
- Final deployment and launch
- CMS editability so our team can maintain normal website content through WordPress/Elementor
Our preferred environment is:
WordPress + Elementor Pro + Hello Elementor
We are open to technically justified recommendations, but we do not want unnecessary plugins or unnecessary custom complexity.
Important Implementation Requirement
We are specifically looking for a developer who understands reusable Elementor architecture.
The website has consistent visual and structural patterns. We expect the developer to establish global styles and reusable templates/components rather than independently rebuilding every page.
The supplied HTML/CSS reference pages should be treated as implementation references/blueprints, not simply embedded into WordPress as static HTML.
The final website should remain appropriately editable through WordPress and Elementor.
Design and Content Control
The website's architecture, approved copy, brand system and major design decisions have already been established.
This project is primarily an implementation assignment, not a redesign or copywriting assignment.
The successful developer should be comfortable working accurately from controlled source documents and raising questions where specifications appear to conflict rather than independently changing approved content.
There are also specific requirements concerning organisational and service-provider attribution that must be followed exactly as supplied.
Forms and Contact Hub
The website includes a central Contact Hub with multiple enquiry pathways, including enquiries relating to:
- Mental Health & NDIS Support
- Referrals / Support Coordinators
- Programs
- Organisations & EAP
- Speaking & Facilitation
- Festivals & Community Events
- Partnerships
- General enquiries
The originating enquiry context needs to be preserved and routed appropriately.
Integrations
The project includes standard integration with:
- MailerLite
- Acuity Scheduling
Please identify any additional paid plugin or licence you believe is genuinely required and explain why.
We prefer to minimise unnecessary ongoing plugin costs.
Accessibility, Responsiveness and Performance
The website should be professionally implemented across desktop, tablet and mobile.
Accessibility should target WCAG 2.2 AA, including appropriate semantic heading structure, keyboard accessibility, visible focus states, form labelling and other relevant front-end accessibility practices.
The website should also be built with sensible performance practices and without unnecessary plugin or code bloat.
Selection Process
Shortlisted candidates may be given controlled access to selected project documentation and our Front-End Release 0.1.1, containing the five reference pages.
We expect to shortlist approximately 2–3 candidates.
Before awarding the full project, we may ask shortlisted candidates to complete a small paid technical trial.
The trial will test the ability to translate part of the supplied reference system into a clean, reusable, responsive and editable Elementor implementation.
This is intended to assess actual implementation capability rather than relying solely on portfolios.
Your Proposal
Please begin your proposal with the exact phrase:
OLH ELEMENTOR 2026
This helps us identify applicants who have read the complete brief.
Please then provide:
1. Your total fixed-price quotation in USD for completing the full project through final deployment/launch.
2. Your estimated total number of hours.
3. Your estimated timeframe for completion.
4. Confirmation that your quotation covers all 27 pages.
5. A clear explanation of what is included in your quotation.
6. Any exclusions.
7. Any paid plugins, licences or third-party costs you believe will be required.
8. Links to three live WordPress/Elementor websites you personally built or substantially implemented, explaining your role on each.
9. A brief explanation of your experience building reusable Elementor systems, global styles, templates and components.
10. Your approach to responsive implementation and web accessibility.
11. Your experience with forms, MailerLite and booking/scheduling integrations.
12. Your approach to WordPress performance and security.
13. Whether you personally will perform the work or whether any part will be subcontracted to another person/team.
14. Confirmation that you would be willing to undertake a small paid technical trial before the full contract is awarded.
Important Technical Question
Please also answer the following:
We will provide five completed HTML/CSS reference pages together with the complete 27-page architecture, approved copy and design system. How would you translate those materials into a reusable native Elementor system without treating the project as 27 independently designed pages?
We are particularly interested in your proposed approach to:
- Elementor global styles
- reusable containers/components
- templates
- responsive behaviour
- maintaining CMS editability
- minimising duplicated work
- maintaining consistency across all 27 pages
Project Structure
- Project type: One-time project
- Contract: Fixed price
- Payment: Through Upwork
- Delivery: Milestone-based
- Website: 27 pages
- Platform: WordPress + Elementor Pro preferred
- Potential paid technical trial: Yes
Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for someone who combines technical competence, attention to detail and good communication.
You do not need to reinvent the website.
We need someone who can take a substantial body of completed planning, design and content work and implement it faithfully, efficiently and professionally.
If you are highly experienced with WordPress and Elementor Pro, understand reusable architecture, and are comfortable working from detailed specifications, we would be pleased to review your proposal.

Our website currently performs very well in GTmetrix:
- Grade A
- 96% Performance
- 99% Structure
- 1.1s Largest Contentful Paint
- 119ms Total Blocking Time

However, Google PageSpeed Insights shows significantly worse results on mobile:
- Performance score: approximately 86
- Accessibility score: approximately 84
- LCP: approximately 3.0s
- FCP: approximately 3.2s
- TTFB: approximately 3.2s

Desktop performance is considerably better, including a TTFB of approximately 0.3s.

Current setup
The website runs on:

- WordPress
- DIVI 5
- Pressable hosting
- WP Rocket
- Imagify for image optimization

We already have a good hosting environment and standard caching/image optimization in place. We therefore need someone who can go beyond installing another optimization plugin and properly investigate. 

What we need

We want you to investigate areas such as:
- Mobile TTFB
- LCP and FCP
- Critical rendering path
- Render-blocking CSS and JavaScript
- DIVI 5 generated assets
- WP Rocket configuration
- Server-side caching and page caching
- CDN/cache behavior if applicable
- Fonts
- Third-party scripts
- JavaScript execution
- Unused CSS / JS
- Above-the-fold content
- Lazy loading
- Database or backend bottlenecks
- WordPress plugins that may affect performance
- Differences between cached and uncached requests
- Any other technical issues affecting Core Web Vitals

We do not want someone who only optimizes the homepage. The solution needs to work properly across the entire website, including internal pages and relevant templates.

We expect you to:
1. Audit the current WordPress setup and performance configuration.
2. Identify the actual causes of the mobile performance issues.
3. Explain clearly what needs to be changed and why.
4. Implement the necessary optimizations.
5. Write clean, high-quality code where custom development is required.
6. Test changes across multiple page types, not only the homepage.
7. Verify that optimizations do not break the website, layout, tracking, or functionality.
8. Re-test the website using Google PageSpeed Insights / Lighthouse and relevant performance tools.
9. Provide a short summary of what was changed and any recommendations for maintaining performance.

We are specifically interested in real improvements, not simply increasing a synthetic score through tricks that negatively affect functionality or user experience.

Requirements
- Minimum 5+ years of relevant WordPress development / performance optimization experience
- Strong experience with Core Web Vitals, PageSpeed Insights and Lighthouse
- Strong knowledge of WordPress frontend and backend performance
- Experience with WP Rocket
- Experience working with page builders such as DIVI
- Comfortable debugging TTFB, LCP, FCP, JavaScript, CSS, caching and server-related issues

- Work as an independent freelancer or as part of a small technical team
- No large agencies

- Honor commitments
- Communicate clearly and proactively if you encounter problems

Please do not send a generic agency proposal.

One of the most important features is making it extremely fast and easy for participating stores to list merchandise. Ideally, a seller could take or upload several photos of an item and AI would create a draft listing for the seller to review, edit, and publish.

Using an existing AI/vision service, the system could assist with the product title, description, category and subcategory, brand when reasonably identifiable, color, style, relevant attributes, search keywords or tags, and potentially a suggested selling price or price range. The seller should always review and approve the information before the listing is published. The goal is to dramatically reduce the amount of time it takes a store to list individual secondhand items.

AI-powered product search is also important. I would like shoppers to be able to describe what they are looking for in normal conversational language rather than relying only on traditional keyword searches and filters. For example, a shopper might type, "I'm looking for a blue Ralph Lauren women's sweater under $50," and the system should understand the request, search the current merchandise available from participating sellers, and return the most relevant matches.

The conversational search should work alongside traditional search and filtering. I would like your recommendation on the best practical way to accomplish this using existing AI and search technology.

Customers should be able to purchase directly through the marketplace. Marketplace commissions and seller payouts should be handled automatically through an appropriate payment solution so that I am not manually collecting money and then paying individual sellers.

Because a customer may purchase merchandise from several different stores, I would also like your recommendation for handling a cart containing products from multiple sellers, including separate seller orders, shipping charges, marketplace commissions, and seller payouts while keeping the checkout experience simple for the customer.

The individual sellers will be responsible for fulfilling and shipping their own orders. Sellers should be able to manage their orders and provide shipping and tracking information through their accounts.

I'm open to WordPress/WooCommerce with a strong multi-vendor marketplace solution or another platform if you believe there is a better approach. I would prefer to use reliable existing marketplace software, plugins, APIs, payment solutions, AI services, and search technology where appropriate rather than custom-building functionality unnecessarily.

At the same time, I want the finished site to look and function like a polished standalone business and be built in a way that allows it to grow.

The type of developer is very important to me. I'm looking for someone who is proactive, resourceful, communicates well, and likes to get things done quickly. I particularly value someone who can take ownership of the technical side, research and solve problems independently, and keep the project moving without requiring a lot of day-to-day direction from me. Of course, I'm available whenever something requires my input, access, approval, or a business decision.

When applying, please tell me about multi-vendor marketplaces or similar platforms you have personally built and provide examples if possible. I'd also like to know what platform and technology you recommend for this project and why, how you would implement the AI photo-to-listing feature, how you would implement the conversational AI product search, how you recommend handling marketplace commissions and seller payouts, and how you would handle purchases involving products from multiple sellers.

Please also include your estimated time to complete the site and have it ready to launch, your fixed-price estimate for the complete project, and any significant ongoing software, AI/API, search, payment, plugin, or hosting costs I should expect.

I'm ready to get started and would prefer someone who has the availability to move quickly and consistently. Speed matters to me, but so does getting it right.

There may also be additional work available for the right person. I have multiple online projects and would love to find a developer I can rely on long-term.
coverLetter:

For the AI photo-to-listing feature, I would integrate OpenAI's GPT-4 Vision API via custom PHP/JS to analyze uploaded photos, extract attributes, and prep a draft listing. For conversational AI search, vectorizing product data using Pinecone or OpenAI Embeddings combined with WordPress search provides that exact natural language capability you described. 

I’ve built numerous complex e-commerce and marketplace setups, ensuring blazing-fast performance and seamless mobile experiences (similar to high-traffic builds like https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/). I take full ownership of the technical roadmap, move fast, and build for scale.

Meta Title → Title field in the Snippet Editor.
Meta Description → Description field in the Snippet Editor.
Focus Keyword → Focus Keyword field in the main Rank Math panel.
Configure one Rank Math Video Schema for that exercise:
Schema Type: Video
Headline: %seo_title%
Description: %seo_description%
Embed URL: the exact Vimeo Embed URL supplied in that exercise’s production sheet.
Content URL and Duration: leave the fields empty when instructed to “Leave Blank.”

title: WordPress / Elementor Developer for Custom WooCommerce Implementation from Figma
description:

The existing WooCommerce environment is already operational and should remain largely intact. Product management, inventory, orders and the current e-commerce infrastructure do not require redevelopment unless a technical reason arises during implementation.

The scope of the first development phase consists primarily of the homepage and product detail page, for both desktop and mobile. Complete Figma designs are available for these pages, together with the supporting design system.

The current Figma design can be reviewed here:
https://www.figma.com/design/WQAkoMWK2LcvqMCIONI7ZE/Untitled?node-id=19-2&t=sJZS393DMj1lTnrn-1

The objective is not simply to reproduce the visual appearance of the Figma files. The final implementation should translate the design into a responsive, performant and maintainable website while preserving the intended interactions and visual behaviour.

The visual design includes several sections that are intended to benefit from subtle motion and interaction during development, such as lighting effects, product carousels, review sections and transitions. These behaviours are not yet fully specified in the current static Figma designs and will therefore need to be developed in collaboration with the design team, while maintaining usability and performance.

The Figma files currently define the visual direction, layout and responsive design. Most screens are static at this stage. During development, selected sections will require subtle motion and interaction to bring the design to life, such as lighting effects, carousels, review movement and transitions. These behaviours will need to be developed in a way that fits the existing visual direction without compromising usability or performance.

A key requirement is maintainability. Wedjis is currently centred around a small number of products, but the assortment will expand over time. Sections should therefore be structured so that imagery, copy and featured products can be updated without requiring major redevelopment. Elementor should remain practically usable for ongoing content management, while custom development can be used where this produces a substantially better result.

Existing website and technical environment:
The existing website has been developed incrementally in Elementor and contains a considerable amount of custom HTML and CSS. Parts of the implementation were created with the assistance of AI development tools, meaning the current front-end structure should not automatically be considered the technical foundation for the redesign.

The selected developer will therefore be expected to assess the existing environment first and determine what can reasonably be retained and what should be rebuilt. A clean implementation is preferred over adding further layers to unnecessarily complex legacy code.

Development can take place in a staging environment, allowing the new pages to be built and tested separately from the live website.

WooCommerce should, where possible, remain unchanged at backend level. The redesign should connect to the existing product and commerce structure rather than introduce unnecessary changes to systems that are already functioning correctly.

Collaboration and design handover:
The UX/UI work has been completed in collaboration with an external designer who can remain available during the implementation phase.

This will be particularly relevant for defining interactions, responsive behaviour and motion that are not yet fully specified in the current static Figma designs. Technical questions regarding the intended design behaviour can therefore be discussed directly within the project rather than requiring the developer to make assumptions.

The development process will be coordinated by Wedjis, with design clarification available where required.

Initial scope:
The current development scope covers the desktop and mobile homepage and the desktop and mobile product detail page, including the relevant WooCommerce functionality, responsive behaviour, animations and interactive components.

Additional pages are expected to follow at a later stage. Blog templates, collection/category pages and other parts of the website are currently being evaluated as part of a separate design phase. Successful completion of the initial project may therefore lead directly to a smaller follow-up development contract.

Before development begins, the selected developer will receive access to the Figma project, the existing website and the relevant WordPress environment. Based on this review, the proposal should outline the recommended technical approach, including which components should remain Elementor-based, where custom development is appropriate and whether any elements of the proposed design present technical or performance concerns.

Particular attention should be given to ensuring that the final implementation remains manageable within WordPress after handover.

Timeline and proposal:
The preferred target is to complete the initial phase before December 2026. This is a target rather than an artificial hard deadline. Proposals should therefore include a realistic delivery schedule based on the actual scope of the Figma designs and existing technical environment.

No fixed project budget has been established at this stage. The intention is to first receive technically informed proposals based on the actual design and implementation requirements rather than setting an arbitrary budget before the scope has been properly assessed.

Both fixed-price and milestone-based structures can be considered.

Relevant applications should include examples of previous Figma-to-WordPress / Elementor implementations, preferably involving WooCommerce and custom interactive or animated front-end work. Please also briefly describe the proposed approach to balancing Elementor-based editing with custom development for a project of this nature.

title: WooCommerce Expert Needed - Dell-Style Guided Purchase Journey / Shopping Workflow
description:
========================================
ABOUT THE PROJECT
========================================

We are looking for an experienced WooCommerce developer or development company to help us improve our online purchasing experience.

We want to build a simple "Guided Purchase Journey" similar to the buying experience used by Dell.

The goal is NOT to build a new ecommerce platform or replace WooCommerce.

Our development priority is:

1. Native WooCommerce functionality FIRST
2. Existing, well-supported WooCommerce or WordPress plugins SECOND
3. Custom development ONLY where needed

We want the simplest, most reliable, and most scalable solution possible.

========================================
WHAT WE WANT
========================================

When a customer selects certain products, such as a laptop, desktop, all-in-one computer, or server, we want to guide them through other products and services they should consider before checkout.

Example journey:

Computer

- Membership, if applicable
- Support / Coverage
- Setup and Data Migration
- Software / Security
- Accessories
- Review
- Normal WooCommerce Checkout

Some categories may have several steps. Other categories may combine multiple recommendations onto one step.

Some WooCommerce products or categories will have NO guided journey and should continue using normal WooCommerce behavior.

The journey should normally be assigned by WooCommerce product category.

Examples:

Laptop - New Computer Journey
Desktop - New Computer Journey
All-in-One - New Computer Journey
Accessories - No Journey

Individual products should also be able to override the category journey if needed.

========================================
DELL EXAMPLE - PLEASE REVIEW
========================================

Dell's shopping experience is the concept we want to follow. We will provide screenshots showing the workflow.

Live Dell example: https://www.dell.com/en-us/shop/servers-storage-and-networking/poweredge-r260/spd/poweredge-r260/pe_r260_tm_vi_vp_sb

The concept is:

1. Select Product
2. Add to Cart
3. Review Support / Warranty / Services
4. Review Accessories
5. Review Other Recommended Items
6. Checkout

We do NOT need to copy Dell's visual design exactly. We want to copy the CONCEPT while making our version simpler, faster, and easier to manage.

The attached screenshots show examples of the Dell workflow we are referencing.

========================================
IMPORTANT - CUSTOMER LOGIN
========================================

Customers should be allowed to begin the guided journey without logging in. An anonymous customer receives the generic journey because we do not yet know what they already own.

When the customer logs in, the journey should re-evaluate their account and remove recommendations that no longer apply.


Example:

A customer adds our Home Membership while shopping anonymously.

They later log into their WooCommerce account.

If they already have an active Home Membership:

- Do not offer Membership again
- Automatically remove the duplicate Membership from the cart
- Keep their other valid selections
- Continue the same journey

Guest checkout will be disabled using normal WooCommerce settings. Customers must have an account before completing checkout.

The Journey Engine itself does NOT control pricing or discounts.

========================================
NATIVE WOOCOMMERCE FIRST
========================================

WooCommerce should continue to control:

- Products
- SKUs
- Pricing
- Discounts
- Inventory
- Customer accounts
- Cart
- Checkout
- Orders
- Taxes
- Shipping
- Payments
- Subscriptions

We do NOT want:

- A custom replacement cart
- A custom checkout
- A second product database
- A second customer database
- A custom pricing engine
- An unnecessarily complicated plugin stack

AJAX can be used to make the journey fast and smooth, but selections should use the real WooCommerce cart.

========================================
EXISTING PLUGINS MUST BE REVIEWED
========================================

Before recommending custom development, we want you to determine whether native WooCommerce or an existing supported plugin can accomplish some or all of this.

Plugins and solutions we have already investigated include:

- Gravity Shop Product Configurator / Gravity Forms
- Studio Wombat Advanced Product Fields for WooCommerce
- WooCommerce-native product recommendation or composite solutions

Gravity Shop example/video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HuqS451PT3A

Studio Wombat multi-step example: https://www.studiowombat.com/blog/how-to-create-multi-step-product-options-in-woocommerce/

We are NOT committed to these plugins. If another established solution is better, please explain why.

We prefer buying and configuring a reliable existing plugin over paying to custom-build functionality that already exists.

Custom development should fill the gaps only when necessary.

========================================
PROJECT PHASES
========================================

We expect this project to develop in approximately three phases.

PHASE 1 - GUIDED SHOPPING JOURNEY

Build the basic Dell-style journey.

Examples of Phase 1 requirements:

- Journeys
- Steps
- Recommendation groups
- Category assignments
- Product overrides
- WooCommerce cart integration
- Login and account re-evaluation
- Membership conditional logic
- Responsive and AJAX customer experience

PHASE 2 - PRODUCT RULES AND ASSOCIATIONS

Add simple rules describing products.

Examples:

- Applies to Account, Location, Device, or None
- Computer, Phone, or Tablet compatibility
- Membership prerequisites
- Existing product or coverage conditions

PHASE 3 - DEVICE, LOCATION AND COVERAGE TRACKING

Later, associate applicable products and services with:

- Customer account
- Household or location
- Computer
- Phone
- Tablet

This phase will include items such as:

- Device IDs
- Location IDs
- Serial number or IMEI validation
- Coverage status
- Device health approval
- Replacement-device coverage transfers

A detailed SOW will be provided to qualified candidates before final quoting.

========================================
EXPERIENCE WE ARE LOOKING FOR
========================================

You should have strong experience with:

- WordPress
- WooCommerce
- WooCommerce architecture and APIs
- Custom WooCommerce plugin development
- PHP
- JavaScript / AJAX
- WooCommerce cart and session behavior
- WooCommerce customer accounts
- WooCommerce Subscriptions and/or Membership concepts
- HPOS-compatible development
- Responsive ecommerce UX
- Evaluating existing plugins before custom development

We are looking for someone who understands WooCommerce architecture, not only front-end WordPress design.

========================================
WHEN YOU APPLY
========================================

Please answer these questions in your proposal:

1. Have you built a multi-step or guided WooCommerce purchasing experience before?

Please provide examples.

2. After reviewing the Dell example, how would you approach this project at a high level?

3. Which native WooCommerce functions or existing plugins would you evaluate BEFORE recommending custom development?

4. If custom development is required, how would you keep it lightweight and compatible with future WooCommerce plugins?

Please do not send only a generic company introduction.

We will provide the detailed SOW and additional workflow screenshots to candidates who demonstrate the appropriate WooCommerce experience.

========================================
OUR MAIN DEVELOPMENT PRINCIPLE
========================================

Native WooCommerce first.
Existing supported plugins second.
Custom development third.

We want the finished system to be:

- Simple
- Fast
- Reliable
- Easy for customers
- Easy for staff
- Easy to maintain
- Highly scalable
- Compatible with WooCommerce and future plugins

The goal is to add a helpful guided buying experience to WooCommerce without creating an unnecessarily complicated WooCommerce store.
coverLetter:
Hi! To answer your questions directly: 

1. Yes, I have built multi-step guided purchasing workflows for WooCommerce using a hybrid of plugins and custom extensions. 
2. My high-level approach aligns with your philosophy: I would first audit plugins like Advanced Product Fields or composite product builders, configure them to hook into category-based rules, and only write custom PHP/AJAX code to bridge the gaps (such as the login state cart re-evaluation and membership deduplication). 
3. I would heavily evaluate Studio Wombat's Advanced Product Fields, WooCommerce Product Bundles, and native composite options before writing custom logic.
4. To keep custom code lightweight and future-proof, I build modular, HPOS-compatible custom plugins using hooks and filters rather than overriding core templates, ensuring seamless WooCommerce updates.

As a senior WordPress and WooCommerce developer with deep experience in custom plugin architecture, PHP, and AJAX, I respect your "native first" approach. 

Would you like to share the screenshots and SOW so we can map out Phase 1?

description:

Overview
We run an established WordPress website (Elementor, live for 6 years) with strong search traction. We've designed a new homepage in Lovable and need it rebuilt natively in Elementor so it looks, behaves and performs like the approved design, without harming our existing SEO, URLs, analytics, integrations or any other page on the site.

Goal
Replace the current homepage with a faithful, fast, mobile-optimised and editable Elementor version of the Lovable design, while protecting everything that currently works.

Scope
Homepage rebuild only with potentially helping me build out the other pages. 

Rebuilding all interactive features in the Lovable version: [forms, sliders, tabs, toggles, calculators, CTAs, booking links, etc.]
Connecting forms and integrations to existing systems: [CRM, email platform, GA4, Tag Manager, Meta Pixel, chat widget, etc.]
Mobile and tablet optimisation
SEO protection, performance optimisation and accessibility checks
Handover documentation
Out of scope (unless agreed in writing as a paid add-on)
Changes to any other page, template or plugin functionality
Copywriting or content rewrites. [We will supply all copy, images and brand assets / The developer may make minor copy edits for SEO with our approval.]
Migration off WordPress or changes to hosting
All other pages must remain visually and functionally unchanged.
Requirements
1. Design reproduction
Closely reproduce the approved Lovable design, including layout, typography, spacing, imagery, colours, animations and responsive behaviour.
Build natively in Elementor. No iframes and no embedding the Lovable app.
Custom CSS/JS is allowed where Elementor can't achieve an effect. It must be commented and documented.
Accuracy test: side-by-side screenshots at 1440, 1024, 768 and 390px widths. Differences over [3px] must be fixed or agreed with us.
Flag early any animations or effects Elementor can't reproduce well and propose a fallback. If an effect harms speed, SEO or accessibility, performance wins.
Load fonts locally and efficiently, and check font licences.
2. Functionality and integrations
Match all interactive behaviour in the Lovable version, including hover states, transitions and scroll effects.
Test every form, link and button end to end, including that submissions arrive and notifications and autoresponders work.
3. Mobile and responsive
Design and test for mobile properly rather than shrinking the desktop layout: tap targets, spacing, image sizes and load speed.
Test on real devices or a reliable device service, including iOS Safari, Android Chrome, desktop Chrome, Safari, Firefox and Edge.
4. SEO protection and improvement
Do not change any existing URL. Any unavoidable change needs our written approval and a 301 redirect.
Preserve or improve the current homepage's title tag, meta description, H1/H2 structure, canonical tag, structured data, internal links and key body copy.
All content must be real, server-rendered HTML text, not injected by JavaScript.
Use descriptive alt text, compressed modern image formats (WebP/AVIF), and lazy loading below the fold (but not for the hero image).
Staging must be set to noindex, and that setting must not carry over to live. After launch, confirm the live site is indexable.
Confirm robots.txt and the sitemap are unaffected, and resubmit the sitemap after launch.
Record a pre-launch baseline (Search Console, key rankings, top pages, PageSpeed) and compare after launch.
5. Performance
Target good Core Web Vitals on mobile (LCP, CLS, INP) and a PageSpeed Insights mobile score of [80+], with before and after results.
Keep plugins, scripts and Elementor bloat to a minimum.
6. Analytics, tracking and privacy
Preserve all analytics, tag manager, pixels, conversion tracking, event tracking and cookie consent behaviour. Verify each fires correctly on the new page.
Forms that collect personal data must comply with the privacy laws that apply to us ([GDPR / Australian Privacy Act / other]).
7. Accessibility
Target WCAG 2.1 AA basics: colour contrast, keyboard navigation, alt text, heading structure and readable tap targets.
8. Editability
We must be able to edit text, images, links and sections in Elementor without breaking the layout.
Use global colours and fonts. No hard-coded content in custom code.
Provide a short handover guide or video walkthrough.
Process
Staging only. No work on the live site until we approve.
Nothing goes live without our written sign-off.
Take a full backup before deployment and keep the old homepage as a draft so we can roll back within minutes.
Deploy at a time we agree (preferably low traffic). Clear all caches and CDN afterwards, then check forms, tracking, indexing and errors immediately.
Monitor Search Console for crawl errors, coverage and ranking changes for [2-4] weeks after launch.
We nominate one approver and will give consolidated feedback within [2] business days.
[2] rounds of consolidated revisions are included. Additional rounds are charged at [rate].
[14/30] days of post-launch bug support are included.
Ownership and Access
We own everything, including code, assets and all licences. The Elementor Pro licence stays in our name.
No new paid or unfamiliar plugins without our approval. Provide a list of everything added.
You'll get a separate staging login with least-privilege access, which we'll remove when the job ends.
The page must work without ongoing dependence on you.
Definition of Done
Matches the approved design within the agreed tolerance at all four breakpoints
All forms and integrations tested and delivering
Tracking verified in GA/Tag Manager
No console errors and no layout shift
PageSpeed mobile target met
No changes to existing URLs, metadata or other pages
Cross-browser and device testing passed
Handover completed
Payment Milestones
[25%] Staging version ready for review
[35%] Revisions signed off
[30%] Live, verified and tracking confirmed
[10%] Released after the post-launch support period ends
Deliverables
Staging site for approval
Live deployment after sign-off
Before/after SEO and speed report
Confirmation that forms and tracking work
Handover guide or video

title: Elementor Pro designer-developer — Figma-first redesign of Locations page, office template, homepage
description:
We're a behavioral health practice in Florida with four offices plus telehealth. Our site runs WordPress + Elementor Pro. We need one experienced person who can BOTH design and implement a focused redesign of how our locations are presented. This is not a full site redesign.

SCOPE: THREE SURFACES, ONE SHARED "OFFICE" TREATMENT

1. /locations/ overview page. We recently removed embedded maps, and the page was built around them. Today the four offices appear twice with inconsistent treatments — once as a text list grouped by region with directions links but no phone numbers, and again as a photo card grid with phone numbers but a directions button that only links to the office page. A general contact block (mailing address, hours, fax) sits between them, and a "Virtual" card shows empty address/phone fields. We want one clear, intentional layout that helps a prospective client quickly see where our offices are, get the address and phone for each, get directions in Google Maps, and choose the right office — with telehealth presented sensibly alongside.

2. Office landing page template. All four office pages are generated from one shared Elementor Theme Builder template using dynamic (ACF) content: office name, hero and intro, location copy, address/phone/hours, a filterable grid of clinicians at that location (~50 clinicians across the four offices), and a photo gallery. The map that used to anchor the contact area is gone, and that area needs to feel complete without it — likely a stronger address/contact treatment with a clear Get directions CTA, but we're open to better ideas. The design must keep working with dynamic office-specific content.

3. Homepage Locations section. A simple teaser: five tiles (four offices + Virtual) with a name and link, plus a "View Locations" button. It should reuse the office treatment from the overview page rather than get a separate design. No other homepage changes are in scope.

PROCESS

Agree on the design first, then build:

1. Review the existing pages and content.
2. Produce 1–2 visual directions, preferably in Figma. Six compositions are enough: overview page, office page, and homepage section — each at desktop and mobile. No standalone design system or pixel-perfect mockups at every breakpoint.
3. We select a direction; up to two revision rounds.
4. Build the approved design in Elementor Pro on a staging copy we provide.
5. Resolve tablet/intermediate responsive behavior during implementation.
6. Verify across all four office pages and the homepage.

CONSTRAINTS — PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING

- WordPress + Elementor / Elementor Pro; use the existing theme and components
- No new plugins; no PHP or theme-file changes
- No custom JS or CSS unless we approve it (small, documented CSS for responsive polish is fine to propose)
- No embedded maps, iframes, external fonts, trackers, widgets, forms, or third-party scripts. Plain outbound links (e.g. Get directions in Google Maps) are fine
- Office content must stay dynamic — no hard-coding office info into the shared template or the homepage section
- Existing copy and photography stay unchanged unless we approve a change
- Must work cleanly at phone, tablet, and desktop widths, with particular attention to 360px

ACCESS

You'll work on a staging copy we provide, never production. We'll reproduce the approved changes in production ourselves, so the quality of the handoff matters.

DELIVERABLES

- Design: 1–2 directions; desktop + mobile of the selected direction for all three surfaces; up to two revision rounds; a Figma view link or editable copy at handoff
- Implementation: completed build on staging; all four office pages and the homepage reviewed; responsive behavior verified at ~360px, 768px, and 1440px; no horizontal scroll or broken layouts
- Handoff: before/after screenshots; a concise list of templates, sections, containers, and widgets changed; important breakpoint-specific settings; any new dynamic fields we need to create (e.g. a per-office directions URL)

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

Clear thinking, good information design, restraint, and responsive execution — not animation or flashy effects. Healthcare experience is useful but not required. Please answer the screening questions specifically; we're not interested in generic agency introductions.

title: Senior Shopify Expert — WooCommerce to Shopify Migration (SEO, Payments, Shipping, Plans)
description:
Senior Shopify Expert — WooCommerce to Shopify Migration (SEO, Payments, Shipping, Plans)
We are migrating an existing WooCommerce (WordPress) store to Shopify and need a senior specialist who has done this end-to-end, not just a CSV import.
This is a migration and a platform advisory project. You must know Shopify at every plan level (Starter, Basic, Grow, Advanced, Plus), what is native versus app-based, and how plan choice affects payments, shipping, staff seats, reporting, B2B, checkout customization, and total cost of ownership.
CURRENT STORE (edit these lines before posting)

Platform: WordPress + WooCommerce
Store URL: ADD URL HERE
Approx. catalog: ADD product count and variant count
Customers / orders to migrate: yes or no, and date range if known
Languages / markets: e.g. US only, US and Canada, EU
Notable plugins / custom features: subscriptions, wholesale, bookings, memberships, product add-ons, multi-vendor, reviews, loyalty, ERP, 3PL, etc.
Theme / page builder on WordPress: Elementor, Gutenberg, custom, etc.
Current payments: Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net, etc.
Current shipping: flat rate, table rate, live carrier, local pickup, etc.
Target Shopify plan: undecided — we need your recommendation. Or name the plan if already chosen.

WHAT WE NEED YOU TO DO

Audit and plan recommendation


Audit the WooCommerce store: products, variants, attributes, categories, custom fields, pages, blog, reviews, coupons, customers, orders, plugins, and integrations.
Recommend the correct Shopify plan (Basic, Grow, Advanced, or Plus) based on volume, staff seats, locations, B2B needs, checkout customization, API limits, carrier-calculated rates, and payment fee math — not just the monthly price.
Produce a plugin-to-native-feature or plugin-to-app map with monthly app cost estimates.
Flag anything that does not map cleanly: Woo products with more than 3 option types, very high variant counts, custom checkout fields, subscriptions, digital downloads, memberships, complex tax, multi-warehouse.


Data migration


Products: titles, descriptions, SKUs, prices, compare-at, cost, weight/dimensions, inventory, tags, vendor, product type, images with alt text, variant options, metafields.
Collections: map categories and tags to manual and/or automated collections.
Customers: accounts, addresses, tags, notes. Plan the password-reset flow after launch because passwords do not migrate.
Orders, refunds, gift cards, and draft orders as needed.
Coupons converted to Shopify discounts.
Pages, blog posts, authors, publish dates.
Reviews via Judge.me, Loox, Stamped, or equivalent.
Digital files / downloadable products if applicable.
Clean data on the way over: duplicates, draft junk, broken images, inconsistent attributes.


Theme and storefront


Recommend and implement a theme (Dawn-based or a specific premium theme).
Recreate key templates: home, collection, product, cart, blog, content pages.
Navigation, mega menu if needed, search, filters (native or app).
Mobile-first QA. Accessibility and Core Web Vitals awareness.
Brand assets: logo, fonts, colors, policies.


SEO (non-negotiable)


Full crawl of the live Woo site, or work from our export.
Complete old-URL to new-URL map for products, collections, pages, blog, and filtered or paginated URLs as relevant.
Implement 301 redirects in Shopify and document the matrix.
Preserve or rebuild meta titles, meta descriptions, H1s, image alt text, and canonicals.
Handle Shopify URL structure differences. Example: Woo product paths become /products/, categories become /collections/, blog paths change as well.
Submit sitemap in Google Search Console. Set up domain, www versus non-www, and HTTPS.
Tracking: GA4, GTM, Meta Pixel, Google Ads, and any other pixels we use.
Post-launch monitoring plan for 14 to 30 days: 404s, ranking or traffic dips, indexing.


Payments


Advise Shopify Payments versus third-party gateways and the extra Shopify fee by plan. This changes total cost.
Configure checkout: cards, Shop Pay, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and any regional methods we need.
Tax: Shopify Tax versus manual or third-party. VAT, GST, and duties if we sell internationally.
Test live and test-mode transactions, failed payments, refunds, and partial refunds.


Shipping and fulfillment


Shipping zones, profiles, and rates: flat, weight-based, price-based, carrier-calculated.
Shopify Shipping versus own carrier accounts (UPS, FedEx, USPS, DHL) and which plans include live rates.
Local pickup, delivery, free-shipping thresholds, shipping insurance if used.
Multi-location inventory if applicable.
Packing slips, labels, 3PL, ShipStation, or ship-from-store apps if we use them.
Duties and cross-border Markets if in scope.


Apps, automation, and operations


Email: Shopify Email and/or Klaviyo or Omnisend. Transactional plus marketing flows (welcome, abandoned cart, post-purchase).
Shopify Flow / automations for tags, fraud review, fulfillment, low stock.
Inventory and location rules.
Wholesale / B2B if needed: native catalogs versus Plus-only depth versus an app.
Subscriptions if we have them (Shopify Subscriptions, Recharge, or other), including billing-date continuity.
Legal pages: refund, shipping, privacy, terms, cookie consent if required.


Launch and handover


Staging QA checklist and go-live runbook: content freeze, delta import of late orders and customers, DNS A record and CNAME.
Keep Woo online as fallback until Shopify is verified. No double-inventory chaos.
Staff training: admin walkthrough plus a short loom or written SOP.
2 weeks post-launch support for bugs and missed mappings.

REQUIRED EXPERIENCE

Multiple completed WooCommerce-to-Shopify migrations you can show (live URLs plus what you migrated).
Deep Shopify Admin knowledge across all current plans, including what is locked to Grow, Advanced, and Plus: staff accounts, live carrier rates, custom reports, checkout extensibility, B2B catalogs, expansion stores, API limits, third-party payment fees.
Technical SEO for replatforms: redirects, Google Search Console, crawl work — not just copying meta fields.
Payments and shipping configuration in real stores, not demo stores only.
Comfortable with Matrixify, LitExtension, Shopify Importer, or custom CSV/API, and honest about when a tool is not enough.
Liquid, theme editor, metafields, and Checkout Extensibility awareness (Plus only where relevant).
Clear written English and structured communication: weekly status plus a risk log.

Nice to have: Shopify Partner, Plus experience, Klaviyo, subscription migrations, B2B, multi-currency / Markets, 3PL integrations.
HOW WE WILL WORK

Preferred: fixed-price with milestones, or a paid audit first then a fixed build.
Proposed milestones:
Audit + plan recommendation + quote confirmation
Data migration to unpublished or password store
Theme, apps, payments, shipping
SEO redirects + QA
Launch + training + 2-week support

Timeline target: ADD RANGE, for example 3 to 6 weeks, depending on catalog complexity.
Budget: ADD RANGE or ask applicants to propose based on audit. Do not bid a number that assumes a tiny brochure catalog if you have not asked about catalog size.

PLEASE INCLUDE IN YOUR PROPOSAL
Start your proposal with the word REPLATFORM so we know you read the brief.
Then include:

Two or three WooCommerce-to-Shopify migrations (URLs, catalog size, and what was hard).
Which Shopify plan you would lean toward for a store like ours, and why. Cover fees and features, not just “Plus is better.”
The migration tool or tools you prefer and when you would not use an app.
How you handle 301s and post-launch SEO monitoring.
Fixed price or hourly, estimated hours, and what is out of scope.
One risk you see in a typical Woo-to-Shopify move that most freelancers skip.

Do not send a generic “I will migrate your store with 100 percent satisfaction” pitch.
UPWORK SKILLS TO SELECT
Shopify, WooCommerce, Shopify Plus, Shopify Development, Ecommerce Website, Data Migration, SEO, Technical SEO, Payment Gateway Integration, Shipping

title: Transportation Pricing / Booking Functionality
description:
We are looking for a developer with experience building advanced transportation pricing systems for a self-service booking form.

We have an existing website, vehicle categories and pricing structure. We also have a detailed pricing spreadsheet that shows the direction of our current rates.

We need someone who can review the pricing structure, help define the calculation logic, and configure it directly into our website so customers can receive the correct price based on their trip details.

The pricing system needs to account for:

• Different vehicle categories and rates  
• Fixed and distance-based airport transfer pricing  
• Local transportation and disposal packages  
• Base fares with included kilometers and hours  
• Per-kilometer charges  
• Additional hourly charges  
• Outstation and interstate trips  
• Minimum daily kilometer requirements  
• One-way and round-trip calculations  
• Highway and road tolls  
• Interstate and state entry taxes  
• Parking charges where applicable  
• Driver overnight allowances  
• Multi-day bookings  
• Different rates based on trip type, distance and duration  
• Other location-specific transportation charges  

This will be a self-service form. A customer should be able to enter their pickup location, destination, trip type, dates and other required information, select a vehicle, and receive the appropriate price automatically.

For example, for an outstation booking, the system should determine the applicable distance, identify the correct per-kilometer rate for the selected vehicle, apply any minimum kilometer requirement, determine whether an overnight driver allowance applies, and include applicable tolls, state charges and other fees.

We need the developer to understand transportation pricing well enough to identify edge cases and recommend how different fare rules should interact. We do not want someone who will simply copy values from a spreadsheet into the website.

The scope includes reviewing our existing pricing spreadsheet, establishing the pricing logic, building the calculation system, connecting it to the customer-facing booking form, and testing different booking scenarios to confirm that the correct price is generated.

Experience with chauffeur services, taxi platforms, airport transfers, car rental systems, intercity transportation, travel booking systems or similar transportation pricing engines is strongly preferred.

When applying, please share examples of booking systems, fare calculators or transportation pricing engines you have built, and explain what parts of the pricing logic you were responsible for.

Building advanced pricing logic requires more than just translating numbers—it requires anticipating edge cases like minimum daily kilometer rules, overnight driver allowances, toll stacking, and tiered vehicle rates. I specialize in custom WooCommerce development, advanced pricing structures, and building dynamic self-service forms that handle complex, multi-variable calculations smoothly.

title: WordPress Marketing Developer (Full Stack) — Contract, $40/hr
description:
WordPress Marketing Developer (Full Stack) — Contract, $40/hr

Interlaced · Remote · Contract · Starts with a site audit, then up to 5 hrs/week
https://interlaced.io/

The role

Our website changes all the time: new pages, updates to existing ones, and tracking that has to work. Right now we're dealing with slow page loads, broken images, caching issues, and HubSpot conversions that don't reach Google reliably.

We need a developer who owns the site from start to finish. You take a design, build it to match, check your own work, and send us something that's ready to review, not a first draft. You spot problems before we do. And you get work done on your own, without needing a call to make it happen.

If you care about how a site looks and whether its data is right, keep reading.

Your first project: audit and fix

Before any new builds, you'll do a full technical audit of our site:

Performance: find out why pages load slowly and fix it (Core Web Vitals, asset loading, plugin bloat, database cleanup).
Caching: diagnose and fix caching conflicts across WP Engine, plugins, and the CDN.
Images: fix broken images, sizing, compression, and lazy loading.
Tracking and attribution: make sure HubSpot form submissions show up in Google Ads and GA4 as conversions, and that GTM is set up cleanly.
Everything else: plugin conflicts, publishing failures (our blog posts recently stopped publishing correctly), security, and anything else you find.

Audit scope: When you apply, include an estimate of how many hours the audit will take. We'll agree on a set number of hours before you start. The deliverable is a written findings report ranked by impact, with an estimated number of hours for each fix. Then you'll start fixing the most urgent issues right away.

At the same time, you'll build new pages for our AI offering and improve existing pages on the site.

What you'll do after the audit

Front end

Build pages in Divi that match the Figma or design files exactly: spacing, font sizes, image proportions, and how they look on mobile.
Catch and fix visual problems yourself before sending anything for review. If the text size is off or an image is stretched, you fix it first.
Embed and style HubSpot forms so they match the page.
Build pop-ups (with triggers, targeting, and page rules) and modern transitions and animations that don't slow the site down.
Improve existing pages for speed, conversions, and consistency.

Back end

Keep the site fast, stable, and cached correctly on WP Engine.
Own the technical tracking setup: GTM, GA4, Google Ads conversion tags, and HubSpot, all working together, and regularly check that the data is coming through.
Watch for problems before they turn into outages: broken publishing, plugin updates, failed forms, dropped tracking.
Advise on attribution. If something in our setup will skew the data, tell us and suggest a fix.
Must-haves
3+ years building WordPress sites, with strong Divi experience
Hands-on experience with WP Engine (staging, caching, CDN, backups)
Experience embedding and troubleshooting HubSpot forms
Working knowledge of GTM, GA4, and Google Ads conversion tracking, including getting HubSpot conversions into Google
A proven record of improving site speed, with before and after numbers
An eye for design. You notice when something looks off.
Strong written communication. You give clear status updates and flag blockers without being asked.
Nice-to-haves
HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP beyond the page builder
Experience with enhanced conversions, consent mode, or offline conversion imports
A background in B2B or SaaS marketing sites
How we work
You work on your own schedule. We'll send clear direction. You deliver without needing a live session to get things moving.
You keep your commitments. When you give a date, you hit it or tell us ahead of time that you can't.
You check your own work. What you send for review is ready to launch.
You keep us updated. A short written update after each work session: what's done, what's next, and what's blocked.
Rate and hours
$40/hr, contract
Audit phase: a set number of hours, agreed before you start, based on your estimate
Ongoing: up to 5 hours per week, including 1 hour set aside for monitoring: site speed, uptime, forms, publishing, and checking that conversions are tracking. The rest goes to page builds and improvements.
How to apply

Send the following:

Two or three WordPress/Divi sites you built or improved, with your specific role on each
A before and after example of a speed improvement (PageSpeed or GTmetrix scores work)
Your estimate of how many hours the audit will take, and what it would cover
Short answers to these scenarios:
Some visitors see certain images on the site load and others don't. How would you troubleshoot it?
A HubSpot form is getting submissions, but Google Ads shows zero conversions. Where do you start?
We push a page update, but some visitors still see the old version. What do you check?
A scheduled blog post didn't publish at its set time. How do you find out why, and how do you keep it from happening again?

Applications without answers to these scenarios won't be considered.
coverLetter:
Hi Interlaced team! I can jump straight into your technical audit, speed optimization, and tracking fixes without needing hand-holding. 

For the initial technical audit (performance, WP Engine caching, broken assets, and GTM/HubSpot tracking), I estimate it will take **5 to 6 hours**. This will cover a comprehensive review of your database bloat, plugin conflicts, CDN/caching layers, and attribution gaps, resulting in a prioritized impact report.

Here are my answers to your scenarios:
1. **Broken images:** I’d check lazy-loading conflicts, mixed HTTP/HTTPS content, CDN asset paths, and broken image URLs in the database/uploads folder.
2. **HubSpot to Google Ads conversions:** I’d start by inspecting GTM triggers on the HubSpot form submission event (e.g., `hsFormCallback`), verifying GA4 event tags, and checking Google Ads conversion linker and tag IDs.
3. **Stale cached pages:** I’d clear object caching, WP Engine page cache, and CDN (Cloudflare/Fastly) rules, while checking for browser caching headers and dynamic plugins bypassing cache.
4. **Missed scheduled post:** I’d check the WordPress Cron system (`wp-cron.php`), server-level cron jobs via WP-CLI, and conflicting caching or caching plugins blocking the pseudo-cron trigger.

Here is a Divi project from my portfolio matching your stack: https://www.snopud.com/ (customized, optimized WordPress build focusing on performance and layout precision).

Let’s get the audit scheduled—when would you like to kick off?

title: WordPress Website Development
description:
Senior WordPress/PHP Developer Needed to Implement Medicare Preventive Services Questionnaire and PDF Reporting Plugin

Project Description

We are developing a customer-facing Five Year Road Map to Medicare Preventive Services.

We already have an initial custom WordPress plugin package, questionnaire structure, preventive-services scheduling logic, branded report design, official logo and example PDF reports. We need an experienced WordPress/PHP developer to review, test, correct, complete and deploy this system on our GoDaddy-hosted WordPress website.

This is not primarily a website-design or Elementor project. The main work involves custom WordPress plugin development, backend calculations, PDF generation, secure data handling, email delivery and production deployment.

How the System Should Work

A customer visits a page on our WordPress website.
The customer completes a multi-step Medicare preventive-services questionnaire.
The system evaluates the answers using programmed eligibility and scheduling rules.
The system calculates a personalized five-year preventive-services schedule.
A branded PDF report is generated automatically.
The customer receives an email with a secure report-download link.
Authorized staff can review submissions and reports through a WordPress administrative dashboard.

Existing Materials

We will provide:

The existing WordPress plugin ZIP
The questionnaire and conditional-question structure
The initial Medicare scheduling engine
The official logo and brand colors
The approved one-page report format
Example completed reports
Instructions describing the intended workflow
Test customer profiles and expected outputs

The selected developer must be comfortable reviewing and improving existing code rather than rebuilding the entire project without first evaluating what is already available.

Required Development Work

Review the existing plugin code and architecture
Install it on a GoDaddy staging WordPress site
Correct PHP, JavaScript, database or WordPress compatibility issues
Complete the questionnaire and conditional-question behavior
Validate form fields and sanitize all submitted information
Review and correct the deterministic scheduling calculations
Ensure dates, age thresholds, frequencies and service histories calculate correctly
Complete server-side branded PDF generation
Ensure the official logo and report table display correctly
Configure secure report storage and download links
Configure WordPress transactional email delivery
Configure authenticated SMTP and test delivery
Complete the WordPress administrative report dashboard
Add appropriate administrative permissions and access restrictions
Create error handling and logging
Test the website on desktop, tablet and mobile devices
Document installation, configuration, backup and update procedures
Deploy the approved version from staging to production

Security and Privacy Requirements

The questionnaire may collect individually identifiable health-related information. The developer must follow secure development practices, including:

HTTPS throughout the workflow
WordPress nonces and server-side validation
Input sanitization and output escaping
Prepared database queries
High-entropy report-access tokens
Role-based administrative access
Administrative multi-factor authentication
Protection against direct access to stored reports
Secure backups
Data-retention and deletion controls
Audit or activity logging
No advertising pixels on questionnaire or report-download pages
No exposure of submitted information in URLs, analytics tools or ordinary WordPress logs

Experience working with HIPAA-sensitive, healthcare, insurance or financial-information systems is strongly preferred. The developer should not claim that the system is “HIPAA compliant” merely because basic security controls are present. Legal and compliance review will be handled separately.

Required Technical Experience

Applicants should have demonstrable experience with:

Custom WordPress plugin development
PHP 8.0 or later
WordPress coding and security standards
MySQL and custom WordPress database tables
JavaScript and AJAX
WordPress shortcodes
WordPress administrative pages
WordPress email and SMTP
Server-side PDF generation
Secure file storage and downloads
GoDaddy WordPress hosting or GoDaddy cPanel
Staging-to-production deployment
Git or another version-control system
Responsive front-end development

Preferred Experience

Healthcare or insurance applications
Health-related questionnaires
Eligibility or rules engines
Automated document generation
Transactional email systems
Privacy-by-design development
Accessibility testing
WordPress penetration testing or security hardening

Required Deliverables

Technical review of the existing plugin
Written list of required corrections
Working questionnaire installed on staging
Validated scheduling engine
Automatic branded PDF generation
Secure customer report delivery
Working email and SMTP configuration
Administrative dashboard
Completed test plan with results
Production deployment on GoDaddy
Source code and final installable plugin ZIP
Installation and administrator documentation
A short post-deployment support period for defects

Testing Requirements

The developer must test multiple profiles, including:

A new Medicare Part B member
A long-time Medicare member
A Medicare Advantage member
An Original Medicare member
Male and female screening profiles
A current smoker
A former smoker
A person who never smoked
A person with diabetes or prediabetes
A customer with unknown service history
Multiple colorectal-screening methods
Missing or incomplete vaccination history
A roadmap beginning in the middle of a calendar year

For each profile, the developer must compare the generated report with the expected results we provide.

Project Approach

We prefer a milestone-based project:

Milestone 1: Code review and staging installation
Milestone 2: Questionnaire and calculation engine
Milestone 3: PDF generation and report delivery
Milestone 4: Administrative dashboard and security controls
Milestone 5: Testing, GoDaddy production deployment and documentation

Do not make production changes before the staging version is reviewed and approved.

When Applying

Please answer the following questions:

Describe two custom WordPress plugins you personally developed.
Have you created server-side PDFs from WordPress data? Which PDF library or method did you use?
Have you deployed a custom WordPress plugin on GoDaddy?
How would you protect customer reports from unauthorized access?
How would you prevent questionnaire information from appearing in analytics or logs?
How would you test a rules engine that calculates future dates?
What information would you need before configuring SMTP?
Have you worked with healthcare, insurance or other sensitive customer information?
Will you personally perform the work, or will it be assigned to another developer?
Are you willing to provide all source code, documentation and deployment instructions?

Please include examples of relevant custom plugin work. General WordPress design portfolios without custom PHP/plugin examples will not be sufficient.

3. Yes, I have deployed numerous custom plugins on GoDaddy environments, including staging-to-production workflows.
