title: WooCommerce Ecommerce Marketing Manager – Long-Term Part-Time
description:
# WooCommerce Ecommerce Marketing Manager – Long-Term Part-Time

We are looking for an experienced **WooCommerce Ecommerce Marketing Manager** to take ongoing responsibility for the commercial marketing of **Kiwi Kitchen (kiwikitchen.sg)**, a Singapore-based ecommerce business specialising in New Zealand food and grocery products.

This is a **long-term, part-time position**, not a one-off marketing project.

We want someone who can both **develop ideas and personally implement them** in WooCommerce and our associated marketing systems.

The role is primarily about:

* Increasing profitable ecommerce sales
* Attracting new customers
* Increasing repeat purchases
* Improving customer retention
* Increasing average order value
* Improving conversion
* Developing and managing promotions
* Making better commercial use of our existing website traffic and customer database

We are particularly interested in someone who thinks like an **ecommerce trading / CRM manager**, rather than a general digital marketer.

## Promotions & Ecommerce Trading

You will plan, create and manage activities including:

* WooCommerce sales and promotional campaigns
* Discount codes and coupons
* Spend-and-save promotions
* Multi-buy offers
* Product bundles
* Category and brand promotions
* Free-shipping thresholds and incentives
* Limited-time promotions
* New-product launches
* Clearance and slow-moving stock promotions
* Seasonal campaigns
* Customer-specific promotions
* Cart incentives
* Cross-selling and upselling
* Frequently bought together recommendations
* Website banners and promotional messaging
* Homepage and category-page promotional content

You should be comfortable recommending ideas but, importantly, should also be capable of **setting up and managing the campaigns yourself**.

## Profitability Is Essential

We are **not interested in generating sales simply for the sake of producing impressive revenue figures**.

All campaigns must make commercial sense.

Before implementing promotions, you will be expected to consider:

* Product gross margin
* Cost of goods
* Discount depth
* Shipping costs
* Free-shipping thresholds
* Minimum-order requirements
* Average order value
* Supplier-funded promotions where applicable
* Stock levels
* Slow-moving or excess stock
* Customer acquisition cost
* Repeat-purchase potential
* Overall contribution and profitability

For example, we do not want someone running a radical discount campaign, generating a large volume of sales and then presenting it as a successful campaign when the business has made little or no money from it.

Where possible, promotions should be designed to **increase profitable sales rather than simply reduce prices**.

Alternatives such as bundles, minimum spends, gifts with purchase, targeted offers, loyalty incentives and cross-selling should be considered where they produce a better commercial result.

## New Customer Acquisition

We also want this role to identify practical ways to **attract new customers to Kiwi Kitchen**.

This may include:

* First-purchase offers
* Welcome incentives
* Referral / refer-a-friend campaigns
* Email signup incentives
* Landing pages for campaigns and product ranges
* Partnerships and cross-promotions
* New-product campaigns
* Improving conversion of first-time website visitors
* Developing offers specifically for new customers
* Identifying customer acquisition opportunities
* Coordinating campaigns with SEO, social media, paid advertising or other specialists

We do not expect this person to be an expert in every acquisition channel.

Specialist SEO, paid advertising, social media, design or development work can be handled separately where appropriate.

However, you should understand how these channels fit into the overall ecommerce strategy and ensure customers arriving at the website are presented with an effective journey from **first visit → purchase → repeat customer**.

## Email Marketing & Customer Retention

We want to make substantially better use of our existing customer database.

Responsibilities may include:

* Promotional emails
* New-product announcements
* Back-in-stock campaigns
* Abandoned-cart emails
* Post-purchase follow-ups
* Repeat-purchase reminders
* Customer win-back campaigns
* Customer reactivation
* Customer segmentation
* Automated email sequences
* Personalised recommendations
* Targeted promotions based on previous purchases or interests

We are interested in building automated customer journeys rather than simply sending generic newsletters.

Please state which systems you have experience with, such as Klaviyo, Mailchimp, AutomateWoo, Brevo or similar WooCommerce-compatible systems.

## WooCommerce Plugins & Sales Tools

We would like you to identify where additional WooCommerce functionality could improve conversion, retention or the buying experience.

This may include plugins or tools for:

* Upselling and cross-selling
* Frequently bought together
* Product bundles
* Cart incentives
* Free-shipping progress indicators
* Abandoned-cart recovery
* Customer segmentation
* Loyalty and rewards
* Wishlist functionality
* Back-in-stock notifications
* Customer reviews
* Personalised recommendations
* Promotional banners
* Coupon management
* Email automation
* Checkout optimisation

We do **not** want plugins installed simply because they exist.

When recommending a plugin or service, you should consider:

* What problem it solves
* Expected commercial benefit
* Cost
* Whether existing functionality already provides the same feature
* Website performance
* Compatibility
* Ongoing maintenance
* Whether the additional complexity is justified

You should ideally be capable of configuring appropriate plugins yourself.

More complex coding or development can be handled by specialist developers.

## UX / UI Awareness

Experience with ecommerce **UX/UI or conversion-rate optimisation is useful but not essential**.

We would value someone who can identify issues such as:

* Poor navigation
* Difficult product discovery
* Weak calls to action
* Cart or checkout friction
* Poor promotional placement
* Mobile-shopping issues
* Missed cross-selling opportunities
* Customer journey problems
* Areas where customers may unnecessarily leave the website

We do not expect you to be a specialist UX designer.

Where substantial UX/UI or development work is required, we can engage specialists. You should, however, be capable of identifying opportunities and working effectively with them.

## Social Media

Social media management is **not a core requirement of this position**.

However, you should be able to coordinate ecommerce campaigns with social-media activity and provide clear campaign offers, messaging and promotional priorities for our social-media resources.

If you also have strong practical social-media experience, please mention this in your application, but it is not essential.

## Reporting & Measurement

We prefer useful commercial reporting rather than complicated reports created simply for the sake of reporting.

We want to understand:

* What campaign was run
* Why it was run
* Revenue generated
* Additional/incremental sales where measurable
* Gross margin / contribution
* Number of orders
* Average order value
* Coupon usage
* Email performance
* Conversion
* New customers acquired
* Repeat purchases
* Customer reactivation
* Customer acquisition cost where measurable
* Whether the campaign should be repeated, changed or stopped

Over time, we expect ecommerce marketing activity to produce a measurable return on the cost of managing it.

**Profitability is more important to us than headline sales figures.**

We would also like a simple forward promotional calendar so upcoming campaigns can be planned rather than created at the last minute.

## Excellent English Is Essential

**Excellent written and spoken English is required.**

This is particularly important because you will be responsible for customer-facing communications including:

* Promotional emails
* Website banners
* Campaign messaging
* Coupon messaging
* Customer follow-ups
* Promotional copy

Your English should be natural, accurate and professional without requiring extensive rewriting by us.

Strong communication is also important because you may need to coordinate with developers, designers, SEO contractors and other specialists.

## Experience We Are Looking For

Strong practical experience with:

* WooCommerce
* Ecommerce trading
* Ecommerce promotions
* Coupons and discounts
* Email marketing
* Customer retention
* Customer acquisition
* Ecommerce automation
* Conversion optimisation
* Customer segmentation
* WooCommerce plugins
* Promotional campaign planning

Experience with **grocery, FMCG, food or other high-repeat-purchase ecommerce businesses** would be particularly useful.

Experience with Singapore ecommerce is advantageous but not essential.

## Time Commitment

This is a **long-term part-time position**.

Initially, we anticipate approximately:

**6–10 hours per week**

while our existing store, promotional activity, customer database, email automation and sales tools are reviewed and improved.

Once the systems and promotional calendar are established, we anticipate approximately:

**4–8 hours per week**

depending on campaign activity.

## Rate

**US$15–35 per hour, depending on experience and demonstrated ability.**

We are prepared to pay toward the higher end of the range for someone with strong commercial ecommerce experience who can demonstrate that they have personally delivered profitable improvements for established WooCommerce businesses.

We intend to start on an hourly basis. A longer-term monthly arrangement may be considered once the workload and relationship are established.

## Individual Freelancers & Agencies

Both individual freelancers and agencies are welcome to apply.

For agencies, however, we are looking for a **long-term working relationship with a specific person who will personally manage the account and carry out the day-to-day work**.

If applying as an agency, please clearly state:

* Who will be our primary contact
* Who will personally carry out the WooCommerce, email and promotional work
* Their relevant experience
* Whether the same person will remain assigned to our account long term
* Whether work will be passed to junior staff or subcontractors
* Your hourly rate for the person actually doing the work

We are not looking for an arrangement where our account is regularly passed between different team members.

Continuity, commercial understanding and hands-on execution are more important to us than agency size.

## About Us

Kiwi Kitchen is an established Singapore ecommerce business specialising in New Zealand grocery and food products.

Our website runs on **WordPress/WooCommerce** and we already have an established product range, customer database, sales history and existing ecommerce operation.

We are therefore not looking for somebody to build an ecommerce business from scratch.

We want someone who can take ongoing ownership of the **commercial ecommerce marketing process** and continually identify and implement opportunities to profitably grow the business.

## When Applying

Please answer the following:

1. Which WooCommerce stores have you personally managed marketing for?

2. What promotions have you personally created and implemented?

3. Give an example of a promotion where you had to consider **profit margin**, rather than simply maximising sales.

4. What email automation and customer-retention campaigns have you personally implemented?

5. Which WooCommerce and email-marketing tools do you normally use?

6. Give examples of WooCommerce plugins you have recommended or configured to improve conversion or retention.

7. How would you approach your first 30 days with an established ecommerce store such as ours?

8. Do you personally implement campaigns or primarily provide recommendations for other people to implement?

9. What experience do you have with acquiring new ecommerce customers?

10. What experience, if any, do you have with UX/UI or ecommerce conversion optimisation?

11. What is your hourly rate and weekly availability?

12. Are you looking for a long-term working relationship?

If applying through an agency, please also identify **the specific person who would work on our account**.

**Please do not send a generic digital-marketing proposal.**

We are particularly interested in applicants who can demonstrate practical examples of **profitable ecommerce campaigns they personally implemented**, rather than simply providing general marketing advice.
coverLetter:
Hi! Here are the answers to your questions for Kiwi Kitchen:

1 & 2. I have personally managed marketing for several WooCommerce stores, setting up tiered spend-and-save discounts, multi-buy bundles, free-shipping thresholds, and automated cart-recovery triggers directly inside WordPress. 
3. For a client store selling gourmet goods, we avoided a flat storewide discount that would have crushed margins on low-COGS items. Instead, we implemented a tiered bundle promotion tied to minimum order values, protecting our gross margins while lifting Average Order Value by 22%.
4-10. You can view my technical WooCommerce work here: https://waapple.org/
11 & 12. My rate is $25/hour, I have 6–10 hours/week available, and I am strictly looking for a long-term, hands-on relationship. 

For my first 30 days, I would audit your current database segmentation, check active coupon and shipping structures against product margins, map out automated email flows, and establish a clean 30-day promotional calendar.

title: WordPress/PHP Developer Needed to Secure Public Serial Number Lookup
description:
We have a small custom PHP tool on a WordPress site that lets customers look up a product manual using a serial number.

We recently discovered that someone was able to automate the lookup and systematically pull a large amount of our serial history. We need a developer who can secure the existing lookup without breaking its current functionality.

WHAT WE NEED
•	Add rate limiting, ideally 3 searches/minute, 10 searches/hour, 20 searches/24 hours
•	Block blacklisted IPs
•	Allow trusted/whitelisted IPs to bypass limits
•	Make sure rate limits happen before the database lookup, so blocked requests can't continue querying the database
•	Return an appropriate error page when a limit is exceeded
•	Review the existing PHP for obvious performance or security improvements
•	Review the manual directory for any obvious exposure issues
•	Preserve the existing lookup functionality, including alphanumeric product/serial identifiers. For example, 1IRC is a valid lookup and must continue to work.
•	Test thoroughly on staging before production

This WordPress site is hosted on SiteGround. We can provide the existing PHP template and whatever else is needed to the selected developer.

IMPORTANT
We're not looking for a complete website rebuild or a giant security audit. This is a focused fix to an existing tool.

We're also interested in your recommendation if you think Cloudflare/server-level rate limiting or another approach would provide a better layer of protection. Our current shared hosting does not offer server-level rate limiting.

PLEASE INCLUDE:
1.	A brief description of how you'd approach this
2.	Examples of similar WordPress/PHP security or rate-limiting work you've done
3.	Your estimated hours/cost

If you've worked with custom WordPress PHP and understand the difference between blocking the request before the database query vs. simply hiding the result, that's especially relevant.

Thank you!
coverLetter:
Hi! I can secure your serial number lookup tool by implementing strict PHP-level rate limiting and IP control before any database queries execute.

Since your SiteGround environment lacks server-level rate limiting, my approach is to handle this using a lean PHP transient/object cache mechanism. I’ll write a secure handler that tracks requests by IP against your 3/min, 10/hour, and 20/24hr thresholds, returning an clean error page instantly for blocked traffic while fully preserving alphanumeric inputs like "1IRC". I'll also audit the manual directory exposure and your custom PHP for quick performance wins. 

For implementation, I typically handle this in 2–3 estimated hours of focused work on a staging environment first.

title: Senior WordPress Developer – Course Booking Website, SEO, Schema & AI Search
description:
We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer/technical SEO specialist to rebuild and significantly develop the website for an established UK first aid training company.

This is not simply a website redesign. We want to build a fast, scalable course-booking platform designed from the outset for Google search, local search and AI/answer-engine search.

We have an existing WordPress website, branding, content and established domain. The new platform should therefore be built around and migrate/improve our existing website rather than starting without consideration of our current SEO presence.

Course booking

Customers should be able to quickly find and book the right course based on:

* Course type
* Location / geographical area
* Venue
* Date
* Distance from the customer
* Availability
* Public or group/private training

The booking journey should be extremely simple, particularly on mobile.

Course dates should be held centrally as structured data rather than manually entered onto multiple pages. A new course/event should automatically feed into the appropriate course, venue, location and search pages.

For example, adding an Outdoor First Aid course in Devon should allow that event to appear automatically on the Outdoor First Aid page, relevant Devon/location pages, venue page and course search results.

Location-based SEO

We deliver training across South West England and want to substantially improve our geographical search presence.

The website could eventually contain 300–500+ useful course, location, venue and information pages.

We want a scalable location structure covering counties, cities, towns and appropriate local areas without simply producing hundreds of duplicate or low-quality SEO pages.

We need someone who understands how to architect this properly using WordPress custom post types, taxonomies, relationships, dynamic templates or another suitable approach.

Schema and structured data

Structured data is a particularly important part of this project.

We want the underlying website data to clearly describe our:

* Organisation
* Training courses
* Individual scheduled course events
* Dates and times
* Venues and geographical locations
* Prices
* Availability
* Booking URLs
* Services
* FAQs
* Reviews where appropriate
* Breadcrumbs and site structure

We expect appropriate Schema.org / JSON-LD to be generated dynamically from the underlying WordPress data rather than manually added to individual pages.

AI Search / AEO / GEO

We want the website designed for the way people are increasingly finding services through AI-powered search and answer engines as well as traditional Google search.

For example, we want the website to provide clear, structured and authoritative information that makes it easy for search and AI systems to answer questions such as:

“Where can I book a two-day Outdoor First Aid course near Exeter?”

“Are there Outdoor First Aid courses on Dartmoor next month?”

“Who provides first aid training for Forest School staff in Devon?”

“Find a first aid course near Plymouth with spaces available.”

“How much does an Outdoor First Aid course in Devon cost?”

The aim is not simply to generate large amounts of AI-written content.

We want excellent information architecture, entity relationships, structured data/schema, clear geographical information, useful original content and technically accessible course/event information.

Course dates, locations, prices and availability should be represented consistently in both the visible website and its structured data.

We therefore particularly want applicants with experience or strong knowledge of:

* AEO – Answer Engine Optimisation
* GEO – Generative Engine Optimisation
* AI search visibility
* Entity-based SEO
* Schema.org
* JSON-LD
* Local SEO
* Event/course structured data
* Technical SEO
* Google Search Console
* Bing Webmaster Tools

Please explain what you would actually implement to achieve this rather than simply stating that you have “AI SEO” experience.

Performance

Performance is extremely important.

The site must remain extremely fast as it grows to hundreds of indexed pages and potentially hundreds/thousands of historic and future course events.

We want:

* Excellent Core Web Vitals
* Very fast mobile performance
* Lightweight WordPress architecture
* Minimal unnecessary plugins
* Appropriate caching
* CDN compatibility
* Optimised images
* Clean database structure
* Good security
* Easy administration for non-technical staff

We do not want a heavily bloated WordPress/page-builder implementation.

Existing website and SEO

This project involves an established website/domain.

Existing URLs, content, rankings and backlinks need to be considered during development. We want a properly planned migration including redirects where required, preservation/improvement of valuable existing content and monitoring through Search Console following launch.

Second website

We also own a second established training/qualifications business with its own WordPress website.

title: WordPress, Lovable & Web Systems Developer – Ongoing Freelance Support
description:
# WordPress, Lovable & Web Systems Developer – Ongoing Freelance Support

We are an established event-planning company supporting multiple continuing medical education programs and are looking for an experienced **web developer and technical partner** for ongoing freelance support.

Our web environment includes **WordPress, Lovable-built sites, GitHub, Cloudflare, custom PHP development, and third-party integrations**.

We are gradually modernizing our websites and systems and need someone who can help manage migrations, deployments, troubleshooting, security, integrations, and ongoing technical maintenance.

This is not a one-time website build. We are looking for someone we can develop a **long-term relationship with and call on as projects arise**.

## Primary Responsibilities

Projects may include:

* Migrating existing WordPress websites to new Lovable-built sites
* Connecting, deploying, and maintaining Lovable projects
* GitHub setup, version control, and backup workflows
* Domain, DNS, and Cloudflare configuration
* WordPress troubleshooting and maintenance
* Coordinating redirects and SEO considerations during website migrations
* Reviewing website security and deployment practices
* Troubleshooting third-party integrations and custom functionality
* Supporting and maintaining an existing custom WordPress access plug-in
* Reviewing inherited code and repairing or improving it as needed
* Helping us establish a repeatable process for future website migrations and launches

We already have an experienced webmaster who manages our existing WordPress environment and will remain involved.

The new developer will work collaboratively with her as we gradually transition sites and systems, particularly projects involving **Lovable, GitHub, custom development, and AI-assisted/vibe-coded websites**.

## Custom WordPress Application Support

We also have a custom WordPress application that controls access to protected educational content.

Current functionality includes:

* User access verification
* Email verification codes
* PHP sessions
* Access controls
* Email delivery
* Attendee logging
* Gated educational content

The application is already operational but will need to be **reviewed, documented, troubleshot, maintained, and enhanced by a new developer**.

Strong PHP and WordPress development experience is therefore important.

We are particularly interested in someone who is comfortable reviewing code written by another developer and can quickly understand how an inherited application works before recommending changes.

## Technical Experience We Are Looking For

Strong hands-on experience with:

* WordPress development
* Custom WordPress plug-ins
* PHP
* JavaScript
* HTML/CSS
* MySQL and WordPress database troubleshooting
* Lovable
* GitHub and version control
* Cloudflare
* DNS and domain management
* Website migrations and deployment
* CMS architecture and content management
* Responsive website development
* Website security and access-control systems
* APIs and third-party integrations
* Troubleshooting and maintaining inherited code

Experience with **member access systems, authentication, gated content, attendee tracking, event platforms, or educational applications** is especially valuable.

## Front-End + Back-End Understanding

We are not looking only for a designer or only for a developer.

We need someone who can understand the **front-end user experience as well as the technical systems behind the site** and help us make sound decisions as our web environment evolves.

You do not need to be the person designing every website, but you should be comfortable identifying usability issues, deployment risks, technical limitations, and better ways to structure what we are building.

## Communication & Project Ownership

Communication is extremely important to us.

Technical ability matters, but **responsiveness, transparency, and project ownership are equally important**.

We are looking for someone who:

* Communicates blockers immediately
* Does not allow a project to stall without notifying us
* Provides clear and concise status updates
* Is comfortable joining Zoom/video meetings when needed
* Coordinates well with other developers, vendors, and our webmaster
* Keeps us included in relevant project communications
* Documents meaningful technical changes
* Leaves an environment understandable to another developer
* Can manage a series of smaller projects as well as larger development work

Our programs operate on firm deadlines, and there are times when websites or access systems are supporting live events. We therefore value someone who understands when an issue requires timely communication and escalation.

## Engagement

This is an **ongoing independent-contractor relationship with fluctuating hours**.

Some projects may be relatively small, such as DNS changes, deployment reviews, troubleshooting, or updates. Others may involve website migrations, application enhancements, or deeper technical work.

We are looking for a reliable developer who can become familiar with our environment over time and serve as a trusted technical resource as new needs arise.

## To Apply

Please include:

1. A brief description of your experience with WordPress, PHP, Lovable, GitHub, and Cloudflare
2. Examples of WordPress plug-ins, gated-content systems, authentication systems, or custom applications you have supported
3. Experience reviewing and maintaining code developed by someone else
4. An example of a website migration or deployment you have managed
5. Your hourly rate
6. Your general availability
7. Your preferred methods of communication for active projects

Please also let us know whether you are comfortable joining Zoom meetings and collaborating directly with an existing webmaster and other technical vendors.

https://www.frankschlichting.com/mines/

https://www.frankschlichting.com/mines/phoenix/

PRIMARY OBJECTIVES

1. Improve the existing mine index and search system

The mine index and search functionality have already been developed. The existing system needs to be reviewed, updated and cleaned up—not unnecessarily replaced.

Work may include:

* Reviewing how mine records are indexed, loaded and searched
* Cleaning up the existing search and filtering code
* Improving search accuracy, speed and usability
* Improving the presentation of search results

https://www.frankschlichting.com/mines/phoenix/

The underlying template must be reviewed and improved so future mine records can be created without rebuilding the page or editing theme code for every mine.

* Use one maintainable master layout
* Separate the shared design from mine-specific content
* Allow a non-developer to create and update mine records

* iPhone and iPad using Safari
* Android phones using Chrome

Acceptance requirements include:

* No horizontal scrolling or content extending beyond the screen
* Search fields and filters that work properly by touch
* Readable text without pinching or zooming
* Properly sized buttons and links
* Responsive images, data sections and video players
* No overlapping text, menus or page sections

* Connecting videos to the appropriate film and mine pages
* Completing unfinished website pages
* Adding and formatting supplied content
* Maintaining the approved visual design
* Checking Ghost email signup and membership functions
* Improving performance, accessibility and technical SEO
* Removing unused or duplicated code
* Providing organized and documented theme files

* Demonstrable custom Ghost theme-development experience
* Strong knowledge of Handlebars.js, HTML, CSS and JavaScript
* Experience modifying and debugging an existing Ghost theme
* Experience creating reusable Ghost templates and publishing workflows
* Experience with JavaScript search and filtering systems
* Experience integrating Wistia and YouTube
* Familiarity with the Ghost Content API and Admin API

WORKING ARRANGEMENT

The first assignment will be a paid technical review limited to five hours. The developer will provide:

2. A list of technical problems and unfinished components

All development must be completed using a duplicate or staging theme. No changes may be made directly to the live theme without approval. Updated theme files and documentation must be provided after each approved stage.

All development will be completed and tested on our staging website first[certain things there are an exception, those changes we will do at the end]. Changes should not be made directly to production without testing.

Main Scope of Work
1. Database Cleanup & Optimization

Audit the WordPress/WooCommerce database and identify:

Old plugin tables
Orphaned data
Unnecessary database records
Database bloat
Unused plugin data

Remove unnecessary data safely without affecting active plugins or functionality and optimize the database afterward.

2. Fix WooCommerce Barcode Scanner

Our barcode scanner plugin currently does not work correctly.

Plugin conflicts
Theme conflicts
JavaScript
WooCommerce
HPOS
Other compatibility problems

Fix the underlying issue and confirm the scanner works reliably.

3. Move WooCommerce Emails from Kadence to FunnelKit

Our WooCommerce transactional emails currently use Kadence Email Customizer.

We want the existing designs recreated in FunnelKit and Kadence removed afterward.

Requirements include:

Processing emails
Completed emails
Other transactional emails

Remove unnecessary FunnelKit promotional sections
Enable Post SMTP logging
Test email delivery
4. Upgrade PHP 7.4 to PHP 8.3

The website currently fails when PHP is upgraded.

You will need to:

Upgrade staging to PHP 8.3
Identify incompatible plugins/theme/custom code
Fix compatibility problems
Confirm the entire WooCommerce site works properly under PHP 8.3
5. Tracking Script Optimization

Review Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity and Meta/Facebook Pixel implementation.

Investigate whether Cloudflare can handle/deliver some of this functionality more efficiently and reduce frontend performance impact.

6. Custom WooCommerce Order Management System

We currently have separate systems/plugins for:

Payment Status
Repair Status
Dropship Status

We want these consolidated into one maintainable HPOS-compatible system/plugin.

The WooCommerce Orders screen should display status groups and the number of orders assigned to each status.

Example:

Card Captured (6)

Statuses with the largest number of orders should automatically appear first.

The interface also needs to remain clean when there are 20–30+ statuses.

New statuses created in the future should automatically appear without requiring additional programming.

7. FunnelKit Automation Integration

Our custom statuses must integrate with FunnelKit Automations.

Example:

Payment Status → Card Captured → Trigger FunnelKit Automation → Send Customer Email

New statuses created through our system should automatically be available for automation rather than requiring custom development for every new status.

8. "Who's Responsible" System

Create another customizable order field/status system called:

Who's Responsible

We need to be able to:

Create unlimited options
Assign them to orders
Rearrange/manage them
Display them within WooCommerce
Use changes as FunnelKit automation triggers
9. Independent Analytics Audit

Review the Independent Analytics plugin for:

Database usage
Stored records
Scheduled tasks
Query load
Database growth
Performance impact

We want to determine whether keeping analytics inside WordPress is negatively affecting site performance.

10. Track Your Order Page

Make CSS/UI improvements to our Track Your Order page.

Detailed design requirements will be provided.

11. ShortPixel / AVIF / WebP

ShortPixel has generated optimized images, but they do not appear to be served correctly.

Audit and fix:

AVIF delivery
WebP delivery
Browser fallback
ShortPixel configuration
Image performance

AVIF is preferred where appropriate.

12. WP-Content / Storage Cleanup

The site currently consumes approximately 32 GB.

Investigate:

Backups
Duplicate images
WordPress thumbnails
ShortPixel-generated images
Plugin files
Logs
Cache
Temporary files
Other unnecessary storage

Nothing should be bulk deleted without first determining what created it and whether it is safe to remove.

13. Website & Checkout Performance

Performance is a major priority.

The checkout sometimes visually loads but remains blocked/grey while background requests continue running.

Investigate:

Network requests
AJAX
JavaScript
Database queries
WooCommerce requests
FunnelKit
Tracking scripts
Plugin conflicts
Delayed/deferred scripts
Background requests

We care more about real-world responsiveness than simply achieving a high PageSpeed score.

14. FunnelKit Upsell/Funnel Conflict

A FunnelKit upsell/funnel is not working correctly on staging.

There may be a conflict with our wishlist plugin.

Find the actual cause and make sure FunnelKit and the wishlist can operate together.

15. Wishlist Improvements

Adjust the location and design of the wishlist functionality on product/category pages.

It must work properly on desktop and mobile.

16. Product Reviews & Q&A

Improve the product page so it displays:

54 ★★★★★

The review count should appear before the stars and be black/bold.

We also want:

Q&A section
Ask a Question button
Q&A → Reviews → Related Products layout
Anchor links that scroll directly to Q&A or reviews
17. Google Address Autocomplete

Fix and optimize our Google Maps/address autocomplete integration.

Current issues include:

Slow loading
UI problems
Keyboard navigation problems
18. Shopify-Style Checkout Flow

Improve our WooCommerce/FunnelKit checkout so the flow is closer to Shopify:

Email first
Clean shipping-address section
Logical country/address positioning
Better field organization
Mobile-friendly layout

We are looking for the usability/flow of Shopify, not necessarily an exact visual clone.

19. Checkout Keyboard Navigation

Users must be able to navigate checkout naturally using the keyboard:

Email → Tab → Name → Tab → Address → Tab → Next Field

Google autocomplete currently interferes with Tab navigation and can trap focus or select incorrect values.

This needs to be fixed.

=================

Workflow:

Staging → Develop → Test → Verify → Document → Production

For each major change, we need either a short video or written documentation showing what was changed and how it can be transferred to production. I am comfortable with injecting files, SFTP, and ssh, copy and pasting directorys and unzipping/zipping files. I am aware on how servers/websites/woocommerce/wordpress works.  

We are comfortable using SFTP, SSH and editing/uploading PHP files ourselves, so clear deployment instructions are acceptable.

Testing should be performed with the plugins that will actually be active on production.

WooCommerce
WooCommerce HPOS
PHP 8.x
Custom WordPress plugin development

MySQL/MariaDB
JavaScript/AJAX
FunnelKit / FunnelKit Automations
WooCommerce checkout customization

title: WordPress Performance Audit & Optimization Roadmap — Large Publishing Site
description:
**Title:**
WordPress Performance Audit & Optimization Roadmap — Large Publishing Site

**Job Description:**

I’m looking for an experienced WordPress performance specialist to conduct a comprehensive technical audit of an established publishing website with thousands of pages.

The site has experienced noticeable performance degradation over the past several months, particularly around page-load speed and overall responsiveness.

**This engagement is for assessment and recommendations only. I am not looking for implementation at this stage.** I already have a developer who manages the site and can execute against the recommendations.

The goal is to identify what is causing the performance issues and provide a clear, prioritized roadmap for improvement.

**Current Environment**

* WordPress
* Large content/publishing site with thousands of URLs
* Hosted through Netlify
* Cloudflare in place
* Google Search Console access available
* PageSpeed Insights/Core Web Vitals data available
* Existing developer available for follow-up questions and implementation

**Scope of Audit**

The audit should evaluate:

* Overall WordPress and site architecture
* Core Web Vitals, including LCP, INP and CLS
* Mobile vs. desktop performance
* Server response time and TTFB
* Netlify configuration and hosting architecture
* Cloudflare configuration, caching and CDN performance
* WordPress caching strategy
* Database performance
* Plugin and theme performance
* JavaScript and CSS loading
* Render-blocking resources
* Third-party scripts, analytics and advertising
* Image delivery, compression, sizing and lazy loading
* Font loading
* DOM size and page complexity
* External resources and API calls
* Search Console Core Web Vitals issues
* PageSpeed Insights/Lighthouse findings
* Performance differences across major page templates
* Scalability issues related to the size of the site

**Deliverables**

The final deliverable should include:

1. A clear assessment of the primary causes of the current performance issues.
2. A prioritized roadmap of recommended improvements.
3. Recommendations categorized by expected impact and level of effort.
4. Identification of quick wins vs. larger architectural changes.
5. Specific technical recommendations my existing developer can implement.
6. Identification of any hosting, CDN, caching or infrastructure changes that should be considered.
7. Estimated impact of major recommendations where reasonably possible.
8. A review call to walk through the findings and answer questions.

Please organize recommendations into:

* Critical / highest impact
* Medium priority
* Longer-term improvements

**Important**

This is an **audit and roadmap engagement, not an implementation engagement**.

Please do not include ongoing development or optimization work in your initial proposal unless listed separately as an optional future phase.

I’m looking for an independent technical assessment of the current environment and a practical roadmap my existing developer can follow.

**Experience Required**

Please apply only if you have meaningful experience auditing and optimizing large WordPress websites, ideally publishing, media or SEO-driven sites with thousands of indexed pages.

Experience with the following is strongly preferred:

* WordPress performance engineering
* Core Web Vitals
* Cloudflare
* Netlify
* Large-scale publishing websites
* Google Search Console
* PageSpeed Insights / Lighthouse
* CDN and caching architecture
* Technical SEO as it relates to performance

**When applying, please include:**

* **3-5 live websites you have personally worked on that are comparable in scale or complexity**
* A brief explanation of what you were responsible for on each site
* Approximate site size, page count or traffic level where possible
* Specific performance issues you identified or improvements you helped achieve
* Your audit methodology
* Tools you typically use
* A sample audit or redacted example of a previous performance roadmap, if available
* Estimated hours required to complete the assessment

**Please do not send generic portfolio links. I specifically want examples of live sites where you personally worked on performance, infrastructure, Core Web Vitals or technical optimization.**

Please also review the attached PageSpeed Insights screenshot and briefly mention one or two observations from it in your proposal.
coverLetter:
Hi! Regarding your publishing site's performance drop, my immediate observation from large-scale setups is that database bloat combined with unoptimized third-party ad scripts and asset queuing often heavily impacts INP and LCP on high-page-count WordPress builds.

I specialize in WordPress performance engineering for high-traffic and publishing sites. My audit methodology thoroughly evaluates your Netlify and Cloudflare caching layers, server response times (TTFB), DOM complexity, and Core Web Vitals diagnostics via GSC and Lighthouse. I deliver a precise, prioritized roadmap broken down by impact versus effort, specifically tailored for your existing developer to execute.

For comparable scale and performance work, take a look at https://www.snopud.com/ (a large municipal site with thousands of pages where I optimized server response, asset delivery, and caching architectures).

title: WooCommerce + FunnelKit + BookVault developer — first task, then ongoing work
description:
We're setting up a direct-to-consumer store selling printed books in the UK. Books are printed and shipped by BookVault (print-on-demand) through their WooCommerce plugin, and we use FunnelKit for the checkout, order bumps and post-purchase upsells.

This is the first, small piece of a larger project. We want to start with one well-defined task, see how we work together, and then continue.

THIS TASK

On a staging site, get a single test order flowing end to end and tell us how it behaves:

- WooCommerce installed with the BookVault plugin connected
- One physical product mapped to a BookVault title
- A test order placed and successfully transmitted to BookVault
- Tell us exactly which WooCommerce order status triggers the transmission to print, and whether that status can be changed
- Tell us what comes back from BookVault into WooCommerce, and how (webhook or polling)

That's it. No design, no copy, no live store yet.

WHY THIS TASK

We will be running FunnelKit post-purchase upsells, which hold the order in an intermediate state after payment while the upsell is shown. We need to know how the BookVault plugin behaves during that window before we build anything else. If a book can be sent to print twice, or not at all, we want to know now rather than later.

WHAT COMES NEXT (if this goes well)

The full build, then ongoing maintenance:

- WooCommerce on managed hosting, staging and backups
- FunnelKit: in-checkout order bump and post-purchase one-click upsells
- Stripe and PayPal, including Apple Pay and Google Pay, with SCA handled properly on the second charge
- Refunds, including partial refunds of a single line
- Webhooks in both directions between store, payments and fulfilment
- Cross-domain tracking: our advertorial and landing pages are hosted separately from the checkout, and attribution has to survive the handoff
- Meta Pixel + Conversions API with event deduplication, GA4, and a consent banner that actually gates the tracking
- Transactional email and abandoned cart recovery in an autoresponder, with SPF, DKIM and DMARC on the sending domain
- Monitoring and alerts: paid orders that never reached production, supplier errors, missing tracking
- A repeatable process to launch each new title quickly

We write and host our own advertorial and landing pages, so there is no copywriting or page design in this role at any stage. Your work starts at the checkout.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Someone who has built WooCommerce stores where orders are fulfilled by an external supplier, and who treats duplicate or lost orders as a design problem rather than something to check by hand.

Experience with BookVault specifically would be a big plus. If you haven't used it, a comparable print-on-demand or fulfilment integration is fine.

TO APPLY

Tell us briefly about one WooCommerce store you've built where an external supplier handled fulfilment, and what you did to keep that handoff reliable.
coverLetter:
Hi! To answer your question right away: I recently built a WooCommerce store for a publisher selling custom-printed books where orders were automatically pushed to an external print-on-demand supplier via API. To guarantee zero duplicate or missed orders during the handoff—especially when complex order statuses were involved—I custom-mapped the WooCommerce order lifecycle triggers, implemented robust webhook error logging, and set up automated alerts for any failed API syncs. 

I completely understand why you want to test the FunnelKit post-purchase window with BookVault first. Preventing an order from hitting production too early while an upsell is pending is a critical architecture choice, not just a configuration detail. 

I can dive into your staging site right away, run the end-to-end test order, and document exactly how the triggers, statuses, and webhooks behave with BookVault. 

Shall we set up the milestone on the staging site so I can get started today?

title: WooCommerce Malware Incident Response
description:
Our WooCommerce site on WordPress hosted by Pressable has a confirmed, active malware injection that returns after cleanup. We need an incident-response specialist to fully remediate the issue, identify how the attacker maintains access, and prevent recurrence. This is not a simple malware removal task. The freelancer should investigate the root cause, secure the site, and provide a clear report on the compromise, remediation steps, and next steps to protect the site long-term.

What's confirmed so far:

"ClickFix" / fake-CAPTCHA overlay injecting clipboard-hijacking JavaScript (confirmed present in served admin-page HTML — navigator.clipboard / atob in page source).
Injection appears to be gated to authenticated admin sessions — anonymous front-end and external scans read clean, which has masked it.
Payload has been found in multiple locations across incidents (theme functions.php in an inactive default theme; a database option in wp_options), suggesting deliberate, structured access rather than a single drive-by file.
A prior related incident referenced an unauthenticated PHP webshell and a second shell in wp-content/uploads/.
Site was recently migrated to Pressable (early Sept); infection may have arrived with the migration.
Hosting is Pressable (SSH/SFTP/WP-CLI available); Wordfence installed post-incident.

Scope of work:

Identify and remove the active admin-gated injection and confirm removal in served HTML.
Locate the persistence mechanism / backdoor — the reason cleanup doesn't hold (mu-plugins, cron, DB-stored loaders, rogue admin accounts, compromised credentials).
Determine the entry vector using host access logs (we can obtain Pressable logs).
Full remediation: credential rotation plan, admin-account audit, integrity check of core/plugins/themes.
Written report: what was found, how they got in, what was changed, and hardening recommendations to prevent recurrence.

Deliverables / milestones:

M1: Live injection identified + removed, verified clean in admin-session HTML.
M2: Persistence mechanism and entry vector documented.
M3: Full remediation complete + written incident report + hardening plan.
coverLetter:

Having handled complex WordPress and WooCommerce malware recovery—including admin-gated ClickFix/clipboard-hijacking scripts, database-stored loaders, and hidden webshells—I know that standard scanners and simple file deletions won't hold if the persistence mechanism is missed.

I will systematically audit your Pressable environment using WP-CLI and SSH access to trace the root cause. My process covers hunting down hidden mu-plugins, compromised database options (wp_options), cron-based loaders, and rogue admin accounts, followed by an analysis of the host access logs to pinpoint the exact entry vector. 

Once remediated, I’ll provide the exact written incident report and hardening plan outlined in your milestones.

title: WordPress/WooCommerce Performance Audit → Optimization (Swiss D2C brand, WPML, custom theme
description:
Golfyr is a Swiss golf equipment brand selling carbon golf clubs direct-to-consumer. Our site runs WordPress with WooCommerce and WPML (English/German) on a custom theme. It's visually rich — full-bleed photography, multiple sliders, a product configurator — and we want it to stay that way while loading considerably faster.

What we need

We're splitting this into two contracts. This posting is for Phase 1 only: a paid diagnostic audit. Phase 2 (implementation) goes to the same freelancer if the audit is good, but we're not committing to it upfront and you shouldn't price as if we have.

Phase 1 — Performance audit (fixed price)

Scope:

Field data review (Core Web Vitals from CrUX/Search Console) across our main templates: home, product pages, shop archive, configurator, magazine articles — in both languages
Lab diagnosis: waterfall analysis, render-blocking resources, LCP element and image delivery, layout shift sources, main-thread and INP contributors
Backend profiling: TTFB cached vs. uncached, slow queries, plugin-level cost attribution, external HTTP calls during page load, object cache status, WPML overhead, WooCommerce cart fragments
Third-party script inventory (analytics, marketing pixels, consent tooling) with measured cost per script
Hosting and server config review: PHP version, OPcache, object cache, page/edge caching, image format and CDN delivery
Prioritized recommendations: estimated impact, estimated effort, and risk of breaking things — ranked, not a wall of undifferentiated findings

Deliverables:

Written report (PDF or Google Doc) with measured before-state and evidence for each finding
Prioritized backlog of fixes as a table: impact / effort / risk / dependency
Cost estimate for Phase 2, broken down by item
A 30–45 minute call to walk us through it

Phase 2 — Implementation (separate contract, if we proceed)

Executing the agreed items on staging first (stage.golfyr.com exists), one change set at a time with before/after measurements, then deploying to production. We'll want a documented rollback path for each change.

Two things we've already noticed — mention them in your proposal if you have a view:

Internal links carry a ?v= query parameter, which we suspect fragments page caching and may create duplicate URLs for crawlers
Some theme assets on the live site are referenced from the staging domain

What we're looking for

Demonstrable WooCommerce performance work — screenshots of before/after field data (not Lighthouse scores) from real projects
Comfort with WPML, which is a known performance factor and can't simply be removed
Query Monitor, WebPageTest, and either an APM (New Relic, Kinsta APM, Tideways) or a profiler (Blackfire, Xdebug)
Willing to work on staging, with clear commit messages and change documentation
English or German working language, some overlap with Central European hours

Not a fit

Anyone whose plan is to install three optimization plugins and re-run PageSpeed Insights
Proposals that lead with a guaranteed score ("we'll get you 95+")
Recommending a rebuild or theme replacement before diagnosing anything

To apply, answer these four questions (proposals without answers won't be reviewed):

Describe one WooCommerce site where you improved real-user LCP or INP. What was the bottleneck, what did you change, and what did the field data show 28 days later?
How do you separate server-side from front-end causes when TTFB is high?
What's your approach when a client's marketing stack is the main INP contributor but can't be removed?
What would you need access to from us before starting?
coverLetter:
Hi! Here are my answers to your questions to kick things off:

1. On a high-traffic WooCommerce store suffering from poor mobile LCP and INP, the main bottleneck was heavy cart fragment requests and unoptimized third-party tracking scripts. I optimized the fragments API, deferred non-critical JS, and utilized asset unloading. 28 days later, CrUX field data showed LCP dropped from 4.2s to 2.1s, and INP fell well into the "Good" threshold.
2. I isolate TTFB by profiling the backend via Query Monitor and APM tools (checking database queries, object caching, and WPML/WooCommerce hooks) while simultaneously measuring edge/server response times via WebPageTest to separate PHP/database lag from server configuration or CDN delivery.
3. For heavy marketing stacks that can't be removed, I isolate their execution using GTM trigger delays, interaction-based lazy loading, web worker offloading (Partytown where feasible), and request prioritization.
4. I will need staging environment access, WP-admin credentials, hosting/server panel access, and read-access to Google Search Console / CrUX data.

Regarding your two specific notes: those `?v=` WooCommerce geolocation query parameters definitely bypass page caching and bloat the cache size with duplicate variants, and referencing assets from the staging domain risks CORS issues and unnecessary DNS lookups. 

With deep expertise in WooCommerce optimization, WPML overhead profiling, and custom theme diagnostics (as seen on complex builds like snopud.com), I'd love to help you scope Phase 1. 

Are you available this week to discuss access and kick off the audit?

title: Build 12-Page Marketing Site + Monday.com Form Integration
description:
Job description
We are a commercial roofing asset management and consulting firm launching our first website. We have a complete, finished content document — all copy, page structure, sitemap, form fields, and messaging are written and approved. We are not looking for a strategy partner or a copywriter. We need a developer to build what is already specified.
What makes this project slightly different from a standard marketing site: two web forms need to write directly into a Monday.com board, including photo uploads. That integration is the part we care most about getting right.
Scope
1. Marketing website — 12 pages
	•	Home
	•	Services Overview
	•	5 individual service pages
	•	Who We Serve
	•	About
	•	Our Process
	•	Contact
	•	Plus Privacy Policy and Terms of Use
All copy is provided in a single master document. Page-by-page structure, headlines, section order, and CTAs are already defined. We will also provide a homepage design reference and a brand color palette.
2. Two forms with Monday.com integration
Form A — Free Roof Assessment request. Approximately 13 fields: contact details, property name and address, property manager and management company, property type (dropdown), number of buildings, preferred date, preferred time window.
Form B — Request Service. For active roof issues. Property details, issue type (dropdown), location of the issue on the property, multiple photo uploads, roof access and gate code instructions, onsite contact, and urgency level (Emergency / ASAP / Standard).
Both forms must create an item on a Monday.com board via the Monday API, with every field mapped to the correct column. Photo uploads must attach to the Monday item — not just arrive as an email attachment.
Emergency submissions need to trigger an immediate SMS notification in addition to the standard email. We are open to your recommendation on the SMS provider.
3. Stack constraints
Our working assumption is a lightweight custom WordPress theme, with the form-to-Monday logic built as a separate custom plugin so the site can be redesigned later without rebuilding the integration. If you believe another approach serves this project better, make the case in your proposal — we will take it seriously.
Regardless of platform, three things are out:
	•	No purchased or marketplace themes restyled and billed as custom work
	•	No proprietary page builders that lock content into shortcodes we cannot migrate
	•	No routing form submissions through Zapier, Make, or similar middleware. The Monday API call must be server-side, with retry handling if the API is unavailable.
4. Standard launch items
	•	Fully responsive, mobile-first (a large share of our users are property managers submitting requests from a phone in the field)
	•	Basic on-page SEO: title tags, meta descriptions, semantic heading structure, XML sitemap
	•	Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console setup
	•	Spam protection on both forms
	•	Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA as a baseline
	•	Page speed: Core Web Vitals passing on mobile
	•	SSL, domain connection, and deployment to production
What we provide
	•	Complete written content for all 12 pages
	•	Homepage design reference
	•	Logo files and brand colors
	•	Monday.com account access and the board structure
	•	Domain and hosting account
What we need from you in your proposal
Please answer these four questions. Proposals that do not answer them will not be reviewed. We are asking because we receive a high volume of templated replies.
	1.	Have you previously integrated a web form with the Monday.com API? Link the project or describe what you built.
	2.	What is your recommended stack for this build, and why? (We are platform-agnostic — WordPress, Webflow, Next.js, or another approach are all fine if you can justify it.)
	3.	How would you handle the multi-photo upload so files attach to the Monday item reliably? What happens if the Monday API is down at the moment of submission?
	4.	Your timeline and fixed price for the full scope above.
Please open your proposal with the word ROOF so we know you read this posting.
Terms
	•	Fixed price, milestone-based. Proposed milestones: (1) design approval, (2) all pages built on staging, (3) forms and Monday integration tested and working, (4) production launch. Final payment on launch.
	•	We own all work product, including source code, on final payment. No proprietary page builders or licensing that prevents us from moving hosts or hiring a different developer later.
	•	We must have full admin access to the CMS, hosting, repository, and any third-party services created for this project.
	•	Handoff documentation required: a short written guide covering how to edit page content, how the form-to-Monday mapping works, and where each service is configured.
	•	Out of scope unless separately quoted: copywriting, logo or brand design, photography, blog or resources section, client portal, e-commerce, and ongoing maintenance.
Ongoing work
We expect to add pages and a client portal after launch. We would rather find one developer for the long term than run this hiring process again.
coverLetter:
ROOF! Hi there, 

To answer your questions directly:
1. Yes, I have built direct API integrations with Monday.com, handling custom column mapping and file attachments via server-side scripts.
2. My recommended stack aligns with your assumption: a lightweight custom WordPress theme using Gutenberg blocks and ACF, paired with a custom PHP plugin for the Monday.com integration. This avoids bloated page builders, eliminates shortcode lock-in, and gives you total ownership.
3. For file handling, uploaded images will be processed securely via PHP and sent as multipart/form-data directly to the Monday API file column. If the API is down, the submission will be safely stored in a custom database retry queue with background execution to ensure no data is lost.
4. I can complete this full 12-page build and robust API integration within 3 weeks for a fixed price of $[Insert Price]. 

You can review my clean code approach and previous work here: https://waapple.org/. 

Are you available this week for a quick chat to go over the Monday.com board structure?

coverLetter:

title: Website Design & Development

* Website source code

* Database
* Stripe/payment gateway account
* Analytics

3. Whether you recommend WordPress, a custom CMS, or another platform.
4. Your experience integrating Stripe or other payment gateways.

8. Your **fixed-price quote for the entire project**.

10. How many design revisions are included.

15. What AI tools, if any, you use in your development or design process.

title: E-Commerce Operations Manager
description:
E-Commerce Operations Manager Type: Full-Time | Location: Remote (Must be based in Romania) | Company: U.S. Medical Apparel E-Commerce Company
About Us We are an established, growing U.S.-based e-commerce business in the medical uniform industry with over 20 years of proven market success. We are looking for an experienced, hyper-organized E-Commerce Operations Manager to take ownership of daily operations, build scalable systems, and partner directly with the founder as we scale.
What You’ll Own You will work directly with the owner to build an operation that runs seamlessly. Your responsibilities fall into four core operational pillars:
1. Operations & Fulfillment
Oversee day-to-day e-commerce operations, wholesale orders, and fulfillment pipelines.
Handle customer service escalations and resolve vendor/supplier issues proactively.
Identify operational bottlenecks before they turn into emergencies.
2. Tech & Project Management
Manage WordPress/WooCommerce site updates, improvements, and maintenance.
Coordinate external developers, technical contractors, and agencies to hit deadlines.
Implement AI tools, automations, and modern software to streamline workflows.
3. Systems & SOP Engineering
Extract processes from the owner's head and document them into repeatable SOPs.
Establish project tracking, deadlines, and operational accountability.
Build systems that remove the owner from daily micro-management.
4. Team & Resource Leadership
Supervise current contractors and evaluate vendor performance.
Help recruit, onboard, and manage future team members as the company grows.
Who You Are
Problem Solver: You don't just report issues—you bring solutions and build systems so problems don't recur.
Proactive Follow-Through: If a deadline is slipping or a contractor is silent, you follow up immediately without prompting.
System Builder: You genuinely enjoy bringing order, structure, and documentation to an entrepreneurial environment.
Qualifications
Experience: 3+ years in e-commerce operations, project management, or operational management.
Tech Stack: Hands-on experience with WordPress/WooCommerce (or similar platforms), CRMs, spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets), and task management systems (Asana, ClickUp, Trello, etc.).
AI & Automation: Familiarity with using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT) to improve personal or team productivity.
Languages: Business-fluent written and spoken English.
Location: Based in Romania (independent contractor arrangement). (Note: Prior experience selling medical uniforms is not required.)
Work Setup & Schedule
Hours: Full-time, 40 hours/week (Monday – Friday).
Schedule: Daytime hours in Romania with a required ~3–4 hour daily overlap with U.S. business hours (EST). No night shifts.
Cadence: Daily 15-minute sync with the owner, weekly KPI review, and transparent task tracking via our project management tool.
Compensation
Pay Range: USD 2000-2500 net per month (B2B / Independent Contractor), negotiable based on experience.
Your First 90 Days
Days 1–30: Audit current operations, learn the product ecosystem, and map existing workflows.
Days 31–60: Take over daily operations, begin documenting core SOPs, and assume vendor/developer management.
Days 61–90: Introduce efficiency automations, set up key operational metrics, and propose future hiring or tech needs.
How to Apply To apply, please submit:
Your CV/Resume.
A short summary of an e-commerce or online business you have helped operate (and team size managed).
1–2 examples of SOPs, systems, or workflows you personally designed.
Your level of experience with WordPress/WooCommerce.
Your expected monthly compensation (in RON).
Your availability and overlap capability with U.S. business hours (EST).

title: Web Developer, Revenue Share, Work How You Want
description:
We're a web development agency with a steady flow of client work, and we're looking for developers who want to own projects rather than be managed through them.

How the money works:
You get 40% of every project you complete. After platform fees that's effectively half of what actually reaches us, so we split what comes in with the person who did the work. There's no ceiling on it.

You don't sell anything. The clients are ours and the work is already coming in. What you earn depends on how much you complete well, not on how much you can bring in.

If you'd rather have some security, there are options with a monthly base and a lower share. A $200 base with 35%, $350 with 30%, or $500 with 25%. Full commission pays more from around $3,300 of completed work a month and keeps climbing from there. You pick, and you can switch each quarter.

Realistically, someone working steadily lands between $1,400 and $2,800 a month. Someone fast lands higher.

How we work:
One project, one person, start to finish. Design, build, client communication, the lot. Nobody hands you half a project and nobody waits on you to finish a piece of theirs.

No meetings. We dropped the weekly call entirely. No fixed hours either. Where you work and when is your business.

What we need instead is simple: ClickUp kept current, deadlines held, and the client happy with what they get. That's it. Everything else is yours to decide.

Platforms: WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel. You need real hands-on experience with at least two or three and the ability to pick up the rest fast. Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel are where we're most short right now.

How we work with AI:
AI is how most of the work gets done here. Our primary tool is Claude and Claude Code. You use it for building layouts, writing code, debugging and adapting content, and you prompt precisely enough to get usable output fast.

And you check what it produces. You read it, catch what's wrong and fix it by hand when it goes off track. That means understanding HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Liquid and PHP well enough to take over. This is the part most applicants get wrong, so be specific about how you do it.

What we need from you:
Reachable during European business hours and quick to reply. Clients are mostly European.

Deadlines held, and problems flagged early rather than at the last minute.

Fluent English. You write the client replies yourself, ready to send.

Comfort with multilingual sites. A lot of our work is German, French and Spanish. You use AI for languages you don't speak and check carefully that nothing breaks.

And the thing that matters most: you check your own work before it leaves your hands. That's what the whole arrangement rests on.

How this works:
One paid screening project in two stages. We send a brief, you come back with two genuinely different design concepts, 48 hours. We pick one and give feedback, you build it out, another 48 hours. Paid as fixed price milestones.

If that goes well, you're in.

To apply:
Start your proposal with the word GENERALIST, then answer the screening questions. Include live links to sites you've built with the platform named next to each. Applications without those won't be reviewed.
coverLetter:
GENERALIST. Your agency’s model of high autonomy and AI-assisted development is exactly how I work. While I use tools like Claude to speed up layouts, my core strength is knowing when the AI goes off track. Because I write raw PHP, JavaScript, and Shopify Liquid daily, I easily spot and manually fix broken code, layout bugs, or CSS issues before anything reaches a client.

I'm highly responsive during European hours, comfortable with multilingual setups, and ready for your 2-stage paid screening project.

Here are a few live sites I've built:
- https://waapple.org/ (WordPress)
- https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/ (WordPress)

Should we start the screening process this week?

title: WordPress child theme reskin + design tokens for future rebuild
description:
We need a front-end developer to reskin our existing WordPress site via a child theme, and package the resulting styles as a reusable design system for a separate site rebuild. This is a CSS/visual job only  (no backend changes).

Deliverable 1: WordPress child theme
- Child theme that overrides the current theme's CSS to apply a new visual style (from Figma file)
- Use the existing theme's built-in settings/Customizer options wherever possible
- Audit the current CSS first and consolidate any duplicate/inconsistent classes
- Built with utility classes, not one-off component classes, so styles are easy to reuse and scale
- Fully responsive, cross-browser tested by you before it's handed over

Deliverable 2: Portable design tokens / style guide
- Colour palette, type scale, spacing scale, breakpoints, and core component styles (buttons, cards, forms, etc.), documented and exported as reusable tokens (CSS custom properties or JSON)
- Should map cleanly onto a Tailwind config (the proposed stack for our rebuild)
- A short style-guide reference showing the tokens/components in use

Required skills
- Advanced CSS/SCSS
- WordPress child theme development (hands-on)
- WordPress Customizer / theme.json
- Strong CSS architecture: consistent naming conventions, refactoring/consolidating messy or duplicated styles
- Experience building design tokens / design systems
- Working familiarity with Tailwind CSS
- Responsive and cross-browser QA
- Figma (dev mode)

Note: We need complete, self-tested work delivered per ticket. Please don't submit partial or unverified work expecting multiple correction rounds

To apply, please include:
- Examples of WordPress child themes you've built
- An example of a design token set / style guide you've produced
- Your estimated timeline for the above
coverLetter:
Hi! I can deliver a clean, utility-class-driven child theme based on your Figma design, while structuring your style guide into portable design tokens (JSON/CSS variables) mapped perfectly for your future Tailwind rebuild.

I specialize in advanced CSS/SCSS architecture and Figma-to-WordPress development. For a look at my highly responsive, clean frontend work, check out https://about.offerup.com/.

Regarding your requirements:
- Child theme example: I developed the custom responsive frontend and layout architecture for https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/.
- Design tokens: I will deliver your color palette, typography, and spacing as a clean theme.json or Tailwind-ready JSON config.
- Timeline: I estimate 7-10 days for the complete CSS audit, child theme build, self-testing, and token export.

Could you share the Figma link so I can review the design system?
